title: [FR] internationalization - Customize figure names to set label after number
description:
(Already posted in Stackoverflow [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/54158401/customize-figure-name-just-as-chapter-name-in-bookdown) to no avail.)

Bookdown [allows the customization][1] of chapter names, which is handy when a Hungarian project is built, as `Chapter 1` is translated as `1. fejezet` (i.e. the renaming of `Chapter` is not enough).

However, the very same is true for figure (and table) names as well, because `Figure 1.1` should be translated as `1.1. ábra`, but I don't know how to achieve this (`_bookdown.yml` doesn't seem to support something like "`language/ui/figure_name`" just as it does with `chapter_name`).

There is no problem with the PDF (LaTeX) output, because including `\usepackage[magyar]{babel}` in the `preamble.tex` solves this problem, but I don't know what to do with the non-PDF formats, where my only idea was to use the `_bookdown.yml`.

  [1]: https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/internationalization.html

title: publish_book could offer interactive helper if no argument is set
description:
> Ah ok basically it took a lot of reading to realise that you need to render all book formats before you publish them. Well I tend to think of it like git. If it is a simple vc use and you don't have many branches created, then in most cases I tend to write a customized function that groups git add, commit and push altogether.
> So if a user wants to publish, why do we want to force them to render first, check all formats and then publish. Those who care about format will do it anyways. It is a bit like Microsoft word forcing you to go through all spelling checks before you can save a document if that makes sense.

Same thoughts come in mind with your git example: I would not promote to do git add, git commit, git push because I find it prone to error. However, I see your point. 
If such function would be more verbose by default when used interactively in the IDE, would that be useful to you ? 
It would mean not changing the current default in the function, but if the function is used interactively, it would ask what you want to do with some confirmation. A bit like **usethis** interactivity in a way if you know it. It would allow to present to the user a set of option without needing to really know them before hand. 
Do you think such thing would answer your case ? 

Something like 
```r
> bookdown::publish_book()
--> Do you want to render before publishing ? 
1: All format
2: Only specific
3: Do not render and publish as-is
Selection: 
```

_Originally posted by @cderv in https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/issues/999#issuecomment-717175038_

title: LaTeX workflow fail when figure caption has
description:
Consider

``````
---
title: "Minimal Working Example"
author: "Raniere Silva"
date: "25/03/2021"
documentclass: article
output:
  bookdown::pdf_document2:
    latex_engine: lualatex
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE, fig.cap = "Foo Bar", fig.align = 'center'}
plot(pressure)
```
``````

Compiling the previous document with `Rscript -e 'bookdown::render_book("mwe.Rmd", clean = FALSE)'` with fail and provide the following message

```
! Misplaced alignment tab character &.
<argument> ...hor \expandafter {\@currentHref }{\relax }}Foo&
                                                  nbsp;Bar\fi 
l.92 \caption{Foo Bar}
                         \label{fig:pressure}

Error: LaTeX failed to compile _main.tex. See https://yihui.org/tinytex/r/#debugging for debugging tips. See _main.log for more info.
```

The error is traced back to

``````
```{r pressure, echo=FALSE, fig.cap = "Foo Bar", fig.align = 'center'}
plot(pressure)
```
``````

that is being translated to

```
\begin{figure}

{\centering \includegraphics{_main_files/figure-latex/pressure-1} 

}

\caption{Foo Bar}\label{fig:pressure}
\end{figure}
```

## Proposed solution

Filter the value of `fig.cap` for expressions that might raise issues with LaTeX and others engines.

## Workaround (1)

Based on https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/issues/558.

Users should use `\ ` instead of ` `. For example,

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE, fig.cap = "Foo\ Bar", fig.align = 'center'}
plot(pressure)
```

## Workaround (2)

Users should use ` ` (`#xa0`) instead of ` `. This is undesirable because is hard for users to input and might create some confusion in some users when reading.

## Non-effected Scenarios

If instead of

``````
```{r pressure, echo=FALSE, fig.cap = "Foo Bar", fig.align = 'center'}
plot(pressure)
```
``````

the document has

``````
```{r pressure, echo=FALSE, fig.cap = "Foo Bar"}
plot(pressure)
```
``````

The compilation will be successful. This happens because the code block will be transcript to Markdown instead of LaTeX. For clarification,

```
![(\#fig:pressure)Foo Bar](_main_files/figure-latex/pressure-1.pdf) 
```

instead of

```
\begin{figure}

{\centering \includegraphics{_main_files/figure-latex/pressure-1} 

}

\caption{Foo Bar}\label{fig:pressure}
\end{figure}
```

title: extra_dependencies order in bookdown::gitbook
description:
# Context

I am trying to make a custom output format that adds a few features to the default `gitbook` output (repository [here](https://github.com/InseeFrLab/utilitr-template)). The examples provided here all come from Github Actions build [from this repository](https://github.com/InseeFrLab/utilitr-template) 

Among the things I do, I add some `extra_dependencies` using some custom CSS and JS files (I have very limited knowledge in these two languages. I hope I will not state the obvious). This is [there](https://github.com/InseeFrLab/utilitr-template/blob/8b5021d455be870434c0956a90b48f7a0a9708ab/R/build_website.R#L56). However, when looking at the source code of the generated HTML (an example deployed with Netlify [here](https://awesome-volhard-d6d842.netlify.app/) ), I see that the order is 

```html
<link href="libs/utilitr-default-0.1.0/css/default.css" rel="stylesheet" />
<link href="libs/utilitr-default-0.1.0/css/style-utilitr.css" rel="stylesheet" />
<link href="libs/utilitr-default-0.1.0/css/icones-fa.css" rel="stylesheet" />
<link href="libs/utilitr-default-0.1.0/css/customize.css" rel="stylesheet" />
<script src="libs/utilitr-default-0.1.0/js/book.js"></script>
<script src="libs/jquery-2.2.3/jquery.min.js"></script>
<link href="libs/gitbook-2.6.7/css/style.css" rel="stylesheet" />
<link href="libs/gitbook-2.6.7/css/plugin-table.css" rel="stylesheet" />
<link href="libs/gitbook-2.6.7/css/plugin-bookdown.css" rel="stylesheet" />
<link href="libs/gitbook-2.6.7/css/plugin-highlight.css" rel="stylesheet" />
<link href="libs/gitbook-2.6.7/css/plugin-search.css" rel="stylesheet" />
<link href="libs/gitbook-2.6.7/css/plugin-fontsettings.css" rel="stylesheet" />
<link href="libs/gitbook-2.6.7/css/plugin-clipboard.css" rel="stylesheet" />
```

this means that some elements in our stylesheets might be overriden by elements defined in some stylesheets included in the `bookdown` package. I made an example [there](https://6050e968b9c06b063745988c--awesome-volhard-d6d842.netlify.app/) where I put some elements to define toc appearance in a CSS that is called in `extra_dependencies` ([code there](https://github.com/InseeFrLab/utilitr-template/commit/da1cfbd46e9af54076259be45b29ad75d1bda8a3)). Customized elements, e.g. text color in the TOC, are ignored (when looking at the output in Firefox).

The fix I found to force rendering is to put some elements in a `style.css` stylesheet called in the `_output.yml`. I used this fix to generate the aforementioned [webpage](https://awesome-volhard-d6d842.netlify.app/)  where I modify the appareance of the TOC.

In my opinion, using the `_output.yml` file is not ideal when developping a format within a package. This makes it complicated, for instance, to modify the behavior of the `gitbook` table of content within the package (one cannot assume that the user of the package always add a CSS in the  `_output.yml` YAML). 

# Why it matters ? (in my opinion, I am open to discussion)

I think the order of the dependencies matter because, when using a custom output format, one would expect the classes or properties defined in a few custom CSS to override some default `bookdown/gitbook` classes. Some attributes could still be set as `!important` but I am not sure this would always work. 

## A potential solution ?

I think a partial solution would be to change the order of  `extra_dependencies` in `bookdown::gitbook`  ([here](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/blob/2b7830f1e701df1c459f359c47c06cf3840e441e/R/gitbook.R#L30)) like this is done in `bookdown::bs4_book` ([here](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/blob/2b7830f1e701df1c459f359c47c06cf3840e441e/R/bs4_book.R#L70)):

```r
extra_dependencies = c(gitbook_dependency(table_css), extra_dependencies)
```

## Regarding scripts in `extra_dependencies`

However, I think this does not solve everything regarding JS. Some scripts are present at two locations in the generated HTML. When matching the following pattern, scripts are copied at the bottom of the HTML ([source here](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/blob/2b7830f1e701df1c459f359c47c06cf3840e441e/R/gitbook.R#L133 )):

```r
i = grep('^\\s*<script src=".+/gitbook([^/]+)?/js/[.a-z-]+[.]js"></script>\\s*$', head)
```

The scripts that I would define in `extra_dependencies` will not be duplicated (unless adopting a naming convention, which might be fine). This means you cannot override some functions if you want to change, let's say, the toolbar at the top. 

# Extra

Before posting the issue, I have followed the recommendations ;

- [x] [formatted your issue](https://yihui.org/issue/#please-format-your-issue-correctly) so it is easier for us to read?

- [x] included a minimal, self-contained, and reproducible example?

title: restore_part_html() does not correctly match the tags it removes
description:
Hi, It seems there is an issue with the function [`restore_part_html()`](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/blob/master/R/html.R#L857) in `R/html.R` as called in [`split_chapters()`](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/blob/master/R/html.R#L309) (i.e., with `remove = TRUE`): once the part heading `

` tag is found, the function clears the corresponding line, along with the previous and the next lines (see the `x[i] = x[i - 1] = x[i + 1] = ''` statement on [line 862](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/blob/master/R/html.R#L862)). By doing so, the function expects to remove the `

` tag along with the enclosing `
` tag. However, if there is a comment between the part heading and the following chapter heading in the source file (see the example below), the line following the `

` part heading tag will not be the closing `

` tag, but the first line of the comment. The call to `restore_part_html()` will then remove this line and leave a dangling `` tag (and, maybe, the rest of the comment, which will end up as regular text in the produced HTML, as its opening tag was removed). For instance, the following minimal `index.Rmd` will trigger this issue: ```rmarkdown --- title: "My book" date: "`r Sys.Date()`" --- # My preface {-} Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, and so on. # (PART) My part {-} # My chapter ``` The call to `restore_part_html()` will miss the `` tag and remove the opening ` ``` I guess a solution might be to match the actual opening and closing tags of the enclosing `
` element, but I'm unfortunately not fluent enough in R to propose a patch fixing this. By the way, my R environment: ```r > xfun::session_info('bookdown') R version 4.0.3 (2020-10-10) Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit) Running under: Debian GNU/Linux bullseye/sid Locale: LC_CTYPE=en_US.UTF-8 LC_NUMERIC=C LC_TIME=en_US.UTF-8 LC_COLLATE=en_US.UTF-8 LC_MONETARY=en_US.UTF-8 LC_MESSAGES=en_US.UTF-8 LC_PAPER=en_US.UTF-8 LC_NAME=C LC_ADDRESS=C LC_TELEPHONE=C LC_MEASUREMENT=en_US.UTF-8 LC_IDENTIFICATION=C Package version: base64enc_0.1.3 bookdown_0.21.6 digest_0.6.27 evaluate_0.14 glue_1.4.2 graphics_4.0.3 grDevices_4.0.3 highr_0.8 htmltools_0.5.1.1 jsonlite_1.7.2 knitr_1.31 magrittr_2.0.1 markdown_1.1 methods_4.0.3 mime_0.10 rlang_0.4.10 rmarkdown_2.7.1 stats_4.0.3 stringi_1.5.3 stringr_1.4.0 tinytex_0.29 tools_4.0.3 utils_4.0.3 xfun_0.21 yaml_2.2.1 ``` Thank you very much in advance! title: _output.yml prevents references from being repositioned in pdf_book()
description:
This was previously posted on Stack Overflow, https://stackoverflow.com/questions/66232044/why-does-output-yml-prevent-me-from-moving-references-in-bookdownpdf-book If the root folder contains an `_output.yml` file with an output type of `bookdown::pdfbook:`, then bookdown does not reposition the location of references to where a `
` tag was placed. Instead, running `bookdown::render_book(output_format = 'bookdown::pdf_book')` creates a pdf with a Bibliography inserted at the end of the document and the references listed therein. Removing the `pdf_book` specification from `_output.yml` or deleting `_output.yml` entirely and then running `bookdown::render_book(output_format = 'bookdown::pdf_book')` does correctly place the references where `

title: html_document2: functionality issue when cross-referencing to content in tabbed section
description:
Hi, 
I'm writing a report for which I chose to use the bookdown::html_document2 format because I need the ability to put content in tabs AND to cross-reference properly. So far, everything worked like a charm. Cross-referencing to a figure in a tabbed section produces a correctly numbered link. However, when I click on this link in the rendered output nothing happens. I would have expected the active tab change to the one I was referencing to. title: [FR] Managing redirect
description:
## Context 

I've started a book a couple of months ago, with a series of Rmd, let's say named `chapter-lorem.Rmd`, `chapter-ipsum.Rmd`.

This had generated a book, hosted on GitHub pages, at `myuberbook.org/chapter-lorem.hml` and `myuberbook.org/chapter-ipsum.html`. 

My book has been read and shared on the internet, and potentially people have been sharing links to `myuberbook.org/chapter-lorem.hml`, but now I want to rename it to be `myuberbook.org/lorem.hml`.

## Feature Request

It would be nice to have a native mechanism to do these redirects, in other words having a way to change the chapter URLs, while still keeping the old URL active with a redirect.

A native redirect would allow to: 

- Keep old bookmarks and links "alive", i.e they are still usable
- Be better for SEO (google prefers finding a redirect than a dead link)

My current approach is to, after the book compilation, write a series of HTML files with in it : 

```
<head>
  <meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; URL=lorem.hml" />
</head>
```

using 

```
make_redirect <- function(from, to){
  html <- sprintf(
    '<head><meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0; URL=%s.html" /></head>', 
    to
  )
  dest <- fs::path("_book", from, ext = "html")
  fs::file_create(dest)
  write(html, dest)
}
make_redirect("chapter-lorem", "lorem")
```
--

description:
Following #1048, I open this as way for users to vote for this by giving a 👍 as this is something we could consider in the future.

`bs4_book()` is designed to be used for one chapter per page. The `split_by` won't be changed in the future. 
Organizing a book by one section per page (`split_by = "section"`) will require a new format.
For now, `gitbook()` needs to be used. 

Upvote if you don't like organizing by one page by chapter and you deeply wish there would be a new format designed for this purpose. Thank you for letting us know your interest !

E.g. at the top of https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown-cookbook/indent-text.html I'd like to be able to remember what section 4.12 is without having to click (even if the URL itself that I see on hover is a bit informative).

I think this issue is related to #689.

I don't know how this would work, maybe with [html5 data attributes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/data-*). The feature is also similar to `bs4_book()` making footnotes available on hover.

title: Include Tufte-style margin notes and figures in gitbook/bookdown
description:
Thanks for your work on this excellent package. I'd like to put in a feature request to allow Tufte-style margin notes in gitbook/bookdown. Margin/side notes and figures are possible with the [tufte_html_book()](https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/html.html#tufte-style) output format using `^[footnote content]` or [`margin_note()`](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown/tufte-sidenotes.html) or [`marginfigure`](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown/tufte-figures.html). But I'd prefer to stick with gitbook because gitbook has features that the Tufte style does not, including a floating table of contents. If it's helpful, there are other attempts to adapt gitbook to include margin notes (see below), but it'd be nice for this feature to be integrated into the package for use with gitbook and bookdown.

https://community.rstudio.com/t/bookdown-contest-submission-gitbook-style-tufte-style-for-web-book/11666/6
https://rdrr.io/github/dtkaplan/SDSdata/man/margin_note.html
https://github.com/susanemcg/pandoc-tufteLaTeX2GitBook
https://github.com/CrumpLab/statisticsLab/issues/17

Thanks!

title: Purpose of plugin-highlight.css?
description:
I'm using Bookdown with the Gitbook template. I've noticed that this template contains a **plugin-highlight.css** stylesheet with rules for highlight.js. However, highlight.js is not enabled in the template and the default highlighting seems to user other scripts/styles.

I've now disabled the default highlighting with `highlight: null` in **_output.yml** and added highlight.js myself. When I do this, the template picks up the styles in plugin-highlight.css and these override the highlight.js stylesheet I've added myself.

So I'm wondering: What's the purpose of **plugin-highlight.css** in this template? Is it just a leftover? Or am I supposed to use this template when I use highlight.js, so it matches the Gitbook styles?

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/64646749/bookdown-whats-the-purpose-of-plugin-highlight-css

title: Not an issue, a question on understanding
description:
Please forgive the v basic question. I have recently started using R bookdown, to try write scientific papers. I've read the cookbook and book down guide and looked at examples too. My question isn't about an issue with the code, its that I don't understand' how it works. I've been struggling with this for 5 days now, and thought I should ask for help.  I use rmardown, and understand that, but I don't understand how bookdown 'knows' what to put together. As instructed by the helpsheets, I have several chapters:

an index
01-introduction (mainly free text)
02 methods (mainly tables)
03 results (outputs, graphs, tables)
04 concolusion (free text).
Normally in rmarkdown, every new file I open, I have a 'r set up' chunk where I set the initial global decisions for the doc (echo=TRUE for example) and have YAML in each doc. I also install and load all packages I need for that document. Do I still need to do this in bookdown for each chapter? Or do I do it only once in the index chapter? I just don't quite understand what to put in index and what not to put in the other chapters.

Lastly: If I create a graph in chapter 3 can I put it in chapter 2? Or does it render in order of chapters, and is the better way to have a separate file for all the code for my graphs?

I think the issue is, I don't actually understand the YAML in the examples and what its saying-particularly the output parts (probably also getting confused as I've looked at thesis down too...its all a big mess in my mind now!).

pre .copy button {

}

title: Discrepancy between figure legend parsing in bookdown vs Rmarkdown
description:
I've noticed a different behaviour in the parsing of figure legends between bookdown and Rmarkdown documents I'd been writing using rticles and the ordinary pdf document output then I moved to bookdown. In Rmarkdown newlines are permitted in figure legends with two newlines needed to end the legend but a single newline ends the legend in bookdown, placing the subsequent lines outside the legend. I prefer the behaviour where newlines are allowed as this way I can place each sentence on a newline for easier tracking in git. Would it be possible to harmonize the behaviour of figure legends between Rmarkdown and bookdown to improve the experience of moving between the two?

Rmarkdown:

	```{r afig, fig.cap="(ref:afigCap)", echo=FALSE}
	plot(iris$Sepal.Length, iris$Sepal.Width)
	```
	
	(ref:heynCap) __A predictable Title__ 
	an unsurprising plot (can spread over multiple lines)

Bookdown:
	
	```{r afig, fig.cap="(ref:afigCap)", echo=FALSE}
	plot(iris$Sepal.Length, iris$Sepal.Width)
	```
	
	(ref:heynCap) __A predictable Title__ an unsurprising plot (has to be on one line)

title: Fail early with clear message if book header structure is not the expected one
description:
This follows an investigation from this question
https://community.rstudio.com/t/bookdown-debugging-fixing-incomprehensible-error/87014/6

* The book start with a header h2. By default, `split_by = "chapter"` so a h1 is expected - this fails with a cryptic error (see [community question](https://community.rstudio.com/t/bookdown-debugging-fixing-incomprehensible-error/87014/6))
* If the book start with a header h2 but `split_by: section` is set, the render stop early because of what I believe to be a wrong check 
https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/blob/00987215b7572def2f5cd73a623efc38f4f30ab7/R/html.R#L268-L276
h1 header will always be before h2 header, so if the book start with a h2 header, `h12[1] != i5 + 1` will always be TRUE. I think `sort(h12)` should be done before the `if`

We may need to check the first header found according to `split_by`

* `split_by = "chapter"` => h1 should be first
* `split_by = "section"` => h1 or h2 could be first

Error message should be clear on what is expected.

title: Remove _output.yml and keep all changes in index.Rmd
description:
Suggestion for improvement:

Thanks so much for this fantastic package. As someone who just created his first book from the bookdown-demo template, I think the following feature may reduce the newbie's learning curve:

1. Remove _output.yml so that the user only has to modify index.Rmd to finish necessary customization. The title of the toc and the edit link can be taken from arguments in the index.Rmd header i.e. (title and github-repo)
    - Reason: Take github-repo for example, if one person has edited that in the index.Rmd header, it will be very stressful to figure out why the edit link still directs them to the bookdown repo. I only figured this out by reading [this slide](https://arm.rbind.io/slides/bookdown.html). If the book title is too long for toc title, there can be an argument in index.Rmd heading for `toc-title`?
2. `render_book()` can take in the argument from index.Rmd header and automatically generate all output formats specified and then generate link for download (again remove the need to specify that in _output.yml). 
3. continuing from 2: A more user friendly way may be to present each argument as a TRUE/FALSE option so that the user do not have to dig out what is the command name. (for example, one has to look up the documentation to realise it is not `mobi_book` to produce mobi and not `word_document` to produce docx files. Changing it to TRUE/FALSE or even providing a GUI later on will help a lot of users who just want to get the book published. 
    - Reason: I understand why it is important to allow room for customization as seen from this [pull request](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/pull/53) but I feel that should be more like exceptions rather than default. i.e. most users will probably want books to be generated once they have specified that they want it in the index.Rmd folder and then the download option will be available. Otherwise, it will take three manual steps (specify in index.Rmd, _output.yml, and then run render_book command for that specific format) to get to the ideal results. Basically, it is like turning on a computer and then one has to turn on the mic and speaker manually. Customization is hugely appreciated but the default option should be the most common use case. 
3. In the same vein, `publish_book()` should `render_book()` for all formats by default, and take in the book's name for the name argument. 
4. This might be a big more difficult but if there is a collaborative platform other than GitHub and allows people to edit markdown in its rendered form (e.g. visual editor from mediawiki) it really will help people who co-author books with non-programmers.

Really just my two cents. You have done a fantastic job! Thank you very much!

title: [bug report] move_files_html() does not fully support the CSS specifications for url()
description:
@cderv Following our private convo, here's a bug report. I'm sorry, I haven't sufficient time to follow the issue guide and build a reprex 😢. Feel free to close this bug report!

I have a CSS file that uses an `url()`. I use this CSS file with `bookdown::gitbook()`. Here's an extract:

```css
@font-face {
    font-family: 'Spectral';
    src: url('truetype/Spectral-ExtraLight.ttf') format('truetype');
    font-weight: 200;
    font-style: normal;
}
```

I was surprised because the file `truetype/Spectral-ExtraLight.ttf` wasn't moved in the `lib_dir` directory.

If I don't use quote or use double quotes in the `url()`, the file is correctly moved.

However, the [W3C CSS specifications for `url()`](https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS2/syndata.html#uri) allows the use of single quotes:

> The format of a URI value is 'url(' followed by optional [white space](https://www.w3.org/TR/CSS2/syndata.html#whitespace) followed by an optional single quote (') or double quote (") character followed by the URI itself, followed by an optional single quote (') or double quote (") character followed by optional white space followed by ')'. The two quote characters must be the same. 

To sum up, we have:
- `url(truetype/Spectral-ExtraLight.ttf)` ✔️ 
- `url('truetype/Spectral-ExtraLight.ttf')` ❌ 
- `url("truetype/Spectral-ExtraLight.ttf")` ✔️

I think that the problem comes from this regex: https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/blob/25485d78b8581ceeb66a8c2f199c02300966b070/R/html.R#L1019

title: metadata-file is only available in pandoc >= 2.3, not 2.0
description:
Hi,

The 0.21 bookdown release uses the `--metadata-file` flag to Pandoc.  This is guarded against being used in pandoc 2.0 and lower, but the flag was only introduced in pandoc 2.3.  This means that, for instance, on Debian Stable (which has pandoc 2.2, bookdown attempts to use the flag incorrectly).

If it would help, I can create a PR with a suggested fix (have a `pandoc_2.3` function analagous to the `pandoc_2.0` function to check for that version and bump the requirement in the `R/utils.R` with a check for pandoc 2.3).

Thanks,

Mark

title: Feature: Pre-build search index
description:
In resources/gitbook/js/plugin-search.js, there is the following comment:

```
        // [Yihui] In bookdown, I use a character matrix to store the chapter
        // content, and the index is dynamically built on the client side.
        // Gitbook prebuilds the index data instead: https://github.com/GitbookIO/plugin-search
        // We can certainly do that via R packages V8 and jsonlite, but let's
        // see how slow it really is before improving it.
```

I'm wondering if it is possible to add the ability (or even make it default) to pre-build the search index as mentioned above. I'm dealing with some books that are quite long, and every single page-load has a multi-second delay after load where the page is non-responsive as the search index gets rebuilt. Not surprisingly, it seems that processor gets slammed in the process, too.

title: Having file with only PART header will cause wrong html structure in previous chapter
description:
This comes from an investigation on an issue reported in https://github.com/tidymodels/TMwR/issues/75

# Step to reproduce 

* Use the book demo
* Add a `PART.Rmd` file with this content
```md
# (PART) Content {-}

```
* Use this `_bookdown.yml`
```yaml
book_filename: "bookdown-demo"
language:
  ui:
    chapter_name: "Chapter "
delete_merged_file: true
rmd_files: [
  "index.Rmd",
  "01-intro.Rmd",
  "PART.Rmd",
  "02-literature.Rmd"
]
```
* Build the book

# Issue

The chapter just before the PART header, the one call _Introduction_, will have an incorrect HTML structure leading to

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6791940/95748133-d51e6280-0c99-11eb-9341-42d40409737b.png)

The splitting process of **bookdown** does not handle well this case.

title: Suggested edit to simple table cross-referencing documentation
description:
Given the new interactive table generator in the RStudio preview visual markdown editor, it seems like those sorts of simple tables might get an uptick in use (I find them really handy for generating text-heavy tables, as opposed to trying to shoehorn the content into a dataframe and passing to knitr::kable)

I found the cross-referencing documentation for these types of tables to be a little confusing though. I would suggest something like this instead (this could be updated once the visual markdown editor becomes part of the standard RStudio release to reflect the format created by the interactive table generator?)


Pandoc supports several types of [Markdown tables,](http://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#tables) such as simple tables, multiline tables, grid tables, and pipe tables.  You can write your own simple table directly in markdown like this:

```markdown
Table:(\#tab:simple-table) A simple table in Markdown.
 Sepal.Length   Sepal.Width   Petal.Length   Petal.Width
-------------  ------------  -------------  ------------
          5.1           3.5            1.4           0.2
          4.9           3.0            1.4           0.2
          4.7           3.2            1.3           0.2
          4.6           3.1            1.5           0.2
          5.0           3.6            1.4           0.2
          5.4           3.9            1.7           0.4
```

Which will produce this table when the document is knit

Table:(\#tab:simple-table) A simple table in Markdown.

Sepal.Length   Sepal.Width   Petal.Length   Petal.Width
-------------  ------------  -------------  ------------
          5.1           3.5            1.4           0.2
          4.9           3.0            1.4           0.2
          4.7           3.2            1.3           0.2
          4.6           3.1            1.5           0.2
          5.0           3.6            1.4           0.2
          5.4           3.9            1.7           0.4

You can then cross-reference this simple table using `\@ref(tab:simple-table)`, creating Table.\@ref(tab:simple-table).

https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/blob/74c8bef593c9c365c4d44680d0c0c470c7e38170/inst/examples/02-components.Rmd#L556

title: meta property="og:url" set improperly
description:
The meta property "og:url" should be set to the canonical URL of the *page* you are currently on, not the canonical url of the *site.* (https://ahrefs.com/blog/open-graph-meta-tags/)

Setting the og:url to something other than the current page [tells FB](https://stackoverflow.com/a/7831012/8802249) (and others?) to completely ignore all the data on the current page and scrape the og:url instead.

People should be able to share the particular page of the book they are reading. This doesn't completely prevent that. The link is still correct, but it does prevent the correct *information* from being displayed on FB, forcing every link to a particular page in the book shared on FB to display the info from the /index.html page instead.

You can see the details of what happens if I share the following link to the [YAML Options page](https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/yaml-options.html) of the bookdown book on FB on FB's sharing debugger [here](https://developers.facebook.com/tools/debug/?q=https%3A%2F%2Fbookdown.org%2Fyihui%2Fbookdown%2Fyaml-options.html).

title: cover-image & url wrongly concatenated
description:
When both "cover-image" and "url" options are set in the YAML, the   <meta property="og:image" (and twitter:image and possibly elsewhere) switch from a relative url to an absolute url made by concatenating the two strings. Thus, if the url does not end with a slash, the absolute path to the image is incorrect. 

Thus... 
```
cover-image: "cover.jpg"
url: "https://example.com/book"
```

leads to an output of:

```
<meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/bookcover.jpg" />
```

Whereas it should be:

```
  <meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/book/cover.jpg" />
```

I'm not sure I understand why the cover image url switches from relative to absolute in the first place, but if that's intentional, I believe the concatenation should make sure to add a / if necessary.

title: Support the $$ syntax for pdf output
description:
This is a feature request for `$$` support for pdf output. I'm moving the discussion from https://github.com/rstudio/rticles/issues/326

For epub, [the syntax seems to be supported](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/issues/190#issuecomment-541709385):
``` md
$$
(\#eq:label)
math
$$
```
It would be nice to have it for pdf too.

Because the `$$` notation is closely related to cross-referencing of numbered equations, I think it's relevant to expose the [cross-reference package syntax](http://lierdakil.github.io/pandoc-crossref/#equation-labels).

The cross-reference pandoc filter uses 
```md 
$$ math $$ {#eq:label}
```
Translated to 
```tex
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:label}
math 
\end{equation}
```
for tex output

This is slightly different from the current solution, which is to use a syntax closer to latex
``` rmd
\begin{equation}
(\#eq:label)
math 
\end{equation}
```
This prevents equation previews in Rstudio, and also requires the user to learn a new syntax when outputting to pdf.

title: Custom formatting for figure and table captions
description:
This question was originally posted on [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/63511858/bookdown-figure-number-formatting) and was recommended for a feature request here. By default, bookdown formats figure and table captions as with a colon (`:`) between the figure/table number and the caption: > Figure 2.1: Here is a nice figure! As noted by Yihui on Stack Overflow, this is hardcoded by bookdown in `parse_fig_labels()`. https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/blob/5782b2ffaeea5d6ee7f34562b596d55f70824192/R/html.R#L647-L672 It would be nice to be able to control the separator (e.g., use a `.` or `
` if we wanted the figure/table number and caption on separate lines). Relatedly (but maybe a separate issue), it would also be useful to be able to apply CSS to figure/table numbers and captions separately (e.g., bold figure number and italic caption, [as required by APA](https://apastyle.apa.org/style-grammar-guidelines/tables-figures/figures)). Currently, figure captions are all inside a single paragraph tag (e.g., Figure 2.1 [here](https://bd-reprex.netlify.app/intro.html)), so it's not possible to apply styling to the elements separately. ```html

Figure 2.1: Here is a nice figure!

``` Tables put the table number inside a ``, so it's possible to style the two pieces separately with CSS in HTML output. ```html Table 2.1: Here is a nice table! ``` For both figure and table captions in LaTeX output, the [{caption}](https://ctan.org/pkg/caption?lang=en) package can be used to apply styling to the individual pieces, as well as set the separator. --- By filing an issue to this repo, I promise that - [x] I have fully read the issue guide at https://yihui.org/issue/. - [x] I have provided the necessary information about my issue. - If I'm asking a question, I have already asked it on Stack Overflow or RStudio Community, waited for at least 24 hours, and included a link to my question there. - If I'm filing a bug report, I have included a minimal, self-contained, and reproducible example, and have also included `xfun::session_info('bookdown')`. title: Problem in custom blocks in bookdown of conversion to enumerate for latex/pdf
description:
I posted this question to stackoverflow (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/63144721/problem-in-custom-blocks-in-bookdown-conversion-to-in-enumerate-for-latex-pdf) and am repeating the issue here because I haven't received a response there. What follows is a paste of the question on stackoverflow.

Thanks!

-------------------

I am using `bookdown` in RStudio to compile a series of lecture notes into a single manuscript. I have a custom block that has within it an enumerated list.

````
    ```{r, echo=FALSE}
    instructorVersion<-TRUE
    ```

    The Answer is only for Instructor's Eyes

    1. The answer is hard
    2. You won't get it right
    3. But try anyway
    ```
````

The first block turns out fine in latex:

```
\begin{ANSWER}

\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  This answer is easy
\item
  Yes, really, that's all that I was asking.
\end{enumerate}

```


but for some reason, the second block has a different latex code that creates a problem in compiling

\def\arabic{enumi}.{\arabic{enumi}.} %%% This line is different

I don't have the problem if I use the `:::` Div blocks (the latex code looks like the first one above that compiles correctly).

````

But I am using the ` ```block ` style rather than `::: .{ANSWER}` because I want to be able to toggle on and off whether to have the text appear, as I showed above. I don't know that I can do that with the `:::` format. (I would be happy with an answer that showed me how to use the `:::` version but with a toggle on/off like what I have now.)

Here is my environment command in latex, which basically makes the text red (I don't think it matters, and I've made it just an empty environment and gotten the same thing, but just for completeness)

```
\newenvironment{ANSWER}{%

title: pdf_document2 ignores yaml arguments
description:

```

    toc: true
    number_sections: true
---

# s2

title: Pandoc variables specific to a format could be passed in the format function instead of top level in the YAML.
description:
When trying to use options such as `documentclass`, `lof`, `biblio-title`, `margin-left` or `margin-right` in the preamble of the index/root `Rmd` file, I found that only adding them at the top-level would work:

```yml
site: bookdown::bookdown_site
bibliography: ["Rmd/refs.bib"]
csl: Rmd/ieee.csl
link-citations: yes
documentclass: report
lof: yes
biblio-title: References
margin-left: 35mm
margin-right: 35mm
output:
  bookdown::gitbook:
    config:
      info: no
    bookdown::pdf_book:
      toc_depth: 4
      includes:
        in_header: Rmd/preamble.tex
      latex_engine: xelatex
      citation_package: biblatex
      keep_tex: yes
    bookdown::epub_book: default
```

Instead, I would have expected those keys to be supported in `output > bookdown::pdf_book:`:

```yml
site: bookdown::bookdown_site
bibliography: ["Rmd/refs.bib"]
csl: Rmd/ieee.csl
link-citations: yes
output:
  bookdown::gitbook:
    config:
      info: no
    bookdown::pdf_book:
      toc_depth: 4
      includes:
        in_header: Rmd/preamble.tex
      latex_engine: xelatex
      citation_package: biblatex
      keep_tex: yes
      documentclass: report
      lof: yes
      biblio-title: References
      margin-left: 35mm
      margin-right: 35mm
    bookdown::epub_book: default
```

However, if I use the latter format, those options seem to be silently ignored.

Find full example repo: [LarsAsplund/github-facts](https://github.com/LarsAsplund/github-facts/).

title: Include md files with shifted heading level
description:
Pandoc has a command " shift-heading-level-by= " which dynamically changes all the heading levels on the fly. You can have your content split into small md files and use a builder script to include them. There's a lua filter script which can parse an index.md file for the restructuring of your book, such as 
``` 
{.include shift-heading-level-by=1}
11.md        (in this case, # heading will become ## heading in the output but the 11.md file itself remains untouched)
12.md
```
Bookdown, however, only has a YAML script to include all or some of the md files as they were. Is there a similar mechanic for dynamically set the heading level of an included file?

title: Links in ToC to sections within chapters fail when names are not unique
description:
Creating two sections in different chapters with the same name appears to link all table of contents links back to the *first* section with that name. 

Steps to reproduce:

[bookdown-bug-demo.zip](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/files/4846370/bookdown-bug-demo.zip)

1. Download the demo here: https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/get-started.html
2. In `01-intro.Rmd` add to the end:

```
## Visualisation

Test

```

3. In `02-literature.Rmd` add the same thing to the end (so the section labels are the same: "Visualization".
4. Build using the "Build" button.
5. Open the resulting HTML file and click on the table of contents link for the "Visualization" section of Chapter 3. Notice that it takes you to Chapter 2 instead.

What I expected: The link to the "Visualization" section in Chapter 3 should take you to Chapter 3.

Some things to note:
* Naming the "Visualization" section in `02-literature.Rmd` to "Visualization2" fixes the issue.
* I have confirmed this also occurs with the development version 0.20.1.
* Reverting to bookdown 0.19 fixes the issue.

title: HTML output should default to sans-setif section headings and serif text
description:
In the canonical LaTeX documentclass `book` or `report` for a long-form document (which is `bookdown's` target category), it is desirable to have the body text is typeset using serif version of the font while having the section headings typeset using  sans-serif versions of the font. This appears to be a strong typographical convention for reasons of the comfort of reading.

https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/64059/sans-serif-headings-serif-body-text
http://www.khirevich.com/latex/font/ 
https://subscription.packtpub.com/book/hardware_and_creative/9781847199867/11/ch11lvl1sec155/time-for-action-designing-chapter-and-section-headings 

Right now, looking at the `gitbook` output of the bookdown book as well as the gitbook output generated by `bookdown-minimal` project template, it is not easy to make such a fine-tuned change. The changes of font type currently get applied throughout the document. Can we fine-tune this somehow?

title: .unlisted class not suppressing in table of contents
description:
This is cross-posted from [StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62093984/suppress-r-markdown-heading-from-toc). I have a bookdown project where I would like to exclude a heading from the table of contents. From https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/1625#issuecomment-558854773, and the [R Markdown Cookbook](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown-cookbook/toc-unlisted.html), it appears this should be possible by adding the unlisted and unnumbered classes, e.g.,

```
# Section heading {.unlisted .unnumbered}
```

However, when I apply these classes, only the unnumbered seems to have an effect. That is, the section heading still appears in the TOC, but without a number (i.e., the same effect as `# Section heading {-}`).

A minimal example is in [this repo](https://github.com/wjakethompson/bd-reprex), and the rendered book [here](https://bd-reprex.netlify.app/). title: Figure label printed in the caption using `bookdown::pdf_book()`
description:
When using `bookdown::pdf_book()`, the figure label is automatically printed inside the caption. 

Here is an example R-markdown document.

    title: "Example"
    author: "Paul Hargarten"
    date: "5/22/2020"

    ---

    You can also embed plots (Figure \ref{fig::plots}), for example:
    
    ```{r pressure, echo = FALSE, fig.cap = "\\label{fig::plots} Some caption."}

    ```{r fig.r, fig.pos="h", echo=FALSE, fig.cap="\\label{fig::R} R is a flexible statistical program."}

title: PDF Chapter Preview does not incorporate "includes:" arguments
description:
Despite the [recommendation](https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/preview-a-chapter.html) to only preview to HTML, I sometimes like to preview a bookdown chapter to PDF, so I can print or share with collaborators. I believe the `preview_chapter()` function is failing to incorporate data from the `includes:` YAML option in `_output.yml` when previewing to PDF. 

# Steps to Reproduce:

1. Create a new **bookdown** project (just the minimal project created by 
`File -> New Project… -> Book Project using bookdown` is sufficient for a reprex).

2. Add the following (example) line to `preamble.tex':

   `\DeclareMathOperator*{\argmax}{arg\,max}`

3. Add the following line to a book chapter, for example `03-methods.Rmd`:

   `$$\argmax_f f(x)$$`

4. Compile the full book, confirming that the added LaTeX math line is rendered correctly (`f` centered below `argmax`)

5. Preview the chapter to PDF:

   `preview_chapter('03-method.Rmd', output_format = "pdf_book")`

   This function call will fail, because LaTeX does not know the command `\argmax`, since `preamble.txt` was not added to the document. Inspection of the log file and `.tex` file remaining after the error confirms the absence of the preamble contents. 

Previewing to HTML as normal does not have the issue. Files specified via `includes:` are incorporated appropriately in this case. 

One other observation I made, though I'm not sure it rises to the level of its own bug report: when previewing to PDF via `preview_chapter('03-method.Rmd', output_format = "pdf_book")`, the resulting PDF contains the entire book contents, rather than just the specified chapter, as I would expect. Is this the intended behavior?

title: Error with krantz class and hyperref package (unnumbered sections)
description:
Hi yihui. 
First of all congratulations for your smart package knitr. I'm an R user and I have used this wonderful package in the last two years producing interactive reports. In my opinion this package is a high quality tool for reproducible reseach, as you describe in your book "Dynamic Documents with R and knitr". Now I'm writing my thesis and I have decide to generate the document with knitr and Latex. 
I'm writing you according to report some problems with the krantz class that I have noticed. I'm using the krantz class from this repository that let me to use the hyperref package without compilation problems. I have notice that the hyperref package make the links correct only when I use numbered parts, chapters...
The problem is generated when I use unnumbered commands (\part*{} , \chapter*{}, ...) in the frontmatter and backmatter.
I tryed to fix the problem using \addcontentsline{toc}{chapter}{} together with \chapter*{} and I could show that this works with the standard book class but it doesn't work with krantz class. In this class,  the use of \chapter*{} adds a link in the table of contents that it is not added in the default book class. This behaviour doesn't allow to use the combination of \chapter*{} and \addcontentsline{toc}{chapter}{foo}.
I attached a simple example using your book tamplate in the knitr repository. The links of hyperref are wrong at the first and last sections of table of contents. As you can to show, the preface links in the toc is replicated (one generated by \chapter*{Preface} and the other  generated by \addcontentsline{toc}{chapter}{Author}).
I also attached my actual krantz class. 
I added the following **extra options**:

_-Another page dimensions format (240 x 170)mm.
-Short title option in the headings.
-I commented the definition of cornermarks (I'm not sure if this is the best way to remove the cornermarks)
-I commented \pagestyle{headings} lines (I prefer to set manual the pagestyle in the main document) and I created  \pagestyle{thesisheadings} adding the short title option_ 

Note: I'm not an experienced Latex user. I would appreciate any improvment suggestion

Thanks in advance

title: Mobile (and other small screen devices) experience is not good
description:
I just looked at the sample site https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/ on a cellphone (Samsung Galaxy S8, although I'm certain the same issues are happening with any small screen device) and the results aren't great. As more and more web traffic comes from mobile, I think it's very important to address these issues.

- The "i" icon at the top should be removed because it shows keyboard shortcuts, which are irrelevant for mobile users.
- There are too many icons in the top bar, causing an overflow, so for me the download button and the "i" icon are floating on a separate row below the top bar (screenshot 1)
- The search functionality is very awkward: as you type letters into the search box, if there are any matches on the current page, the entire page is shifted to the right, causing to to not be able to see the characters you typed. You can only see characters you type when no matches on the page are found.  (screenshot 2)

title: hyperref loaded early in pdf_book template conflicts with imakeidx
description:
I am writing a book where I use `imakeidx` to typeset (multiple) indices. The code for including this is located in `preamble.tex` and `afterbody.tex` and those are loaded in `_output.yml` as follows:

```
bookdown::pdf_book:
  includes:
    in_header: preamble.tex
    after_body: afterbody.tex
```

Everything works well except that the indexes are not "clickable" in the PDF. Apparently, that is because `hyperref` is supposed to be loaded last in the document preamble (https://tex.stackexchange.com/a/22014). In my bookdown-setup, `preamble.tex` is included *after* hyperref is loaded (which is done in the pandoc-template for pdf_book, I think), so I have no way of moving my imakeidx code before the loading of hyperref. I tried to make my own pandoc-template but failed to find any documentation how to do this. 

Any help with a solution would be much appreciated!

title: Selection of text from codeblock in Chrome is glitchy
description:

Here is an example from your [example GitBook page](https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/latex.html), below. It is nearly impossible to select single words, single lines or groups of lines, etc.

title: Function render_book does not support passing a path as input
description:
1. Create a folder somewhere in your filesystem: `mybook`.
2. Inside that folder, create a file: `index.Rmd` and write some basic plain markdown.
3. Open the R shell and make sure your working directory (`getwd()`) is not set inside `mybook/`.
4. Invoke, in the shell, Bookdown.

```
bookdown::render_book("path/to/mybook/")
```

### Expected
Bookdown generates the book.

### Actual
Error:

> Error in bookdown::render_book("path/to/mybook/") : 
  No input R Markdown files found from the current directory C:/Users/me/Desktop/mybook or in the rmd_files field of _bookdown.yml

### Rationale
Bookdown is not capable of handling paths, it basically assumes that the working directory is the directory containing the book where the source files are located.

This makes it cumbersome to create libraries building on top of Bookdown. I am trying to create a package that would eventually need to call Bookdown on a folder where I generate some `.Rmd` files. However today I need to use this horrible trick to make things work:

```
cmd = sprintf("setwd('%s');bookdown::render_book('index.Rmd', quiet = %s)", path, TRUE)
Rscript(c("-e", shQuote(cmd)))
```

Unless there is a way to achieve this in a better way, can you change `render_book` to support passing paths?

title: Split bib incomplete in html when using compact numeric citation style
description:
When producing gitbook output using a compact numeric citation style and linked citations, only the first and last reference in the range are shown in the reference list for the page (e.g., refs 1 and 3 when 1-3 are cited). I understand that only the first and last could be _linked_, but expected that all cited refs would be shown. That is, reference 2 (`item2`) should be shown in the reference list but is missing. Is there a setting/workaround to achieve the desired behaviour? If not, I'd suggest that this is a bug.

I'm crossposting from [this SO post](https://stackoverflow.com/q/60909167/489704), which I've bountied without any luck.

title: Redundant removal of attributes on HTML headers
description:
I just noticed that when using Bookdown/Blogdown in combination with Pandoc 2.9+, the following JavaScript dependency gets inserted in the rendered HTML:

```html
<script src="/rmarkdown-libs/header-attrs/header-attrs.js"></script>
```

The content of `header-attrs.js` is found [here](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/blob/master/inst/rmd/h/pandoc/header-attrs.js) and was added with https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/commit/7f51e232c98b2f7db40b40cd593385fe76b3189b.

At the same time, the R function `bookdown:::clean_header_tags()` removes those attributes during rendering (added with https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/commit/a07ae075a92b7031a514f6f31f5f89bd6c84b498).

So – if I didn't miss anything – this header attribute removal is done twice: At first during rendering the R Markdown to HTML using R code (fine) and a second time during rendering the HTML by the browser using JS code (redundant and thus obsolete in the case of Bookdown/Blogdown).

Therefore I think it would make sense to avoid adding this JS dependency when bookdown/blogdown renders a file. Or maybe, the R-based header attribute removal could be performed directly by `rmarkdown::render()` (instead of adding the JS).

(IMHO: The less JS, the better 😬)

title: Allow images or text or pdf pages above first top level heading in bookdown::gitbook:
description:
The example below (i.e. saved as a file index.rmd ) has the same code chunk to display an image above and below the top level heading, but the image doesn't appear above the top level heading. This occurs **if** there is a file _output.yml with only this entry bookdown::gitbook: in the same directory.

That line seems to enforce a table of contents (which I want) and that appears to strip out anything (image or text) before the first top level heading by default (which I don't want) - so can this behaviour be modified?  
````
---
site: bookdown::bookdown_site
---

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(imager)
im <- load.image(system.file('extdata/Leonardo_Birds.jpg',package='imager'))

library(imager)
im <- load.image(system.file('extdata/Leonardo_Birds.jpg',package='imager'))
plot(im, axes=FALSE)
```
````
From a post at rstudio community, I received the option of editing the ```_output.yml``` with

  includes:

```includes``` is an option that will probably work, but it feels unnecessary - how about ```bookdown::gitbook:``` doesn't constrain the user to its ideal scenario of "nothing can exist above the top level header, therefore I will ignore anything that is there" :) - unless there is a really good reason I'm not aware of?

Here is [an example](https://github.com/tamas-ferenci/FerenciTamas_ValszamEsStatAlapvonalai), and here is [the explanation](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/58885889/embedding-a-beamer-presentation-in-a-regular-document-with-rmarkdown/59013249#59013249).)

The problem is that `pdf_book` seems to respect the `output_dir` specified in `_bookdown.yml`, but not the `beamer_presentation`. Thus, when hitting the `Build Book` button, the presentation won't get into the `docs` directory, it'll appear in the base directory.

Is there any way to make `beamer_presentation` respect the `output_dir` specification?

(Also, it'll mean that something has to be done with the filenames, as by default the the names would be the same.)

(Posted in Stackoverflow [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/59644896/having-a-beamer-presentation-and-a-pdf-book-in-the-same-bookdown-project).)

Serif not working when fonts change in style.css
description:
The option to toggle between sans-serif and serif using the font-setting button doesn't work when I change the fonts in style.CSS. Any suggestions?

See StackOverflow: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/59336752/serif-not-working-when-bookdown-fonts-change-in-style-css

The issue seems to happen in a range of examples of published bookdown sites. The issue can be reproduced using other CSS examples, such using: https://github.com/hebrewseniorlife/bookdownThemeEditor 

See also:https://stackoverflow.com/questions/29274501/r-markdown-changing-font-size-and-font-type-in-html-output

This seems to happen when I change fonts for the main text, such as:

_output.yml

```
bookdown::gitbook:
  css: style.css
```

style.CSS

```
p {
  font-family: Arial;
}
```

But not all text changes. For example, if you change just the font for lists, the button still works fine.

style.CSS

li {
  font-family: Arial;
}

The button itself seems to work fine, toggling between the class  `.font-family-1` = sans-serif and `.font-family-0` = serif

title: Feature request: Auto-link function help pages in `gitbook`
description:
By filing an issue to this repo, I promise that

- [x] I have fully read the issue guide at https://yihui.org/issue/.
- [x] I have provided the necessary information about my issue.
    - If I'm asking a question, I have already asked it on Stack Overflow or RStudio Community, waited for at least 24 hours, and included a link to my question there.
    - If I'm filing a bug report, I have included a minimal, self-contained, and reproducible example, and have also included `xfun::session_info('bookdown')`. I have upgraded all my packages to their latest versions (e.g., R, RStudio, and R packages), and also tried the development version: `remotes::install_github('rstudio/bookdown')`.
    - If I have posted the same issue elsewhere, I have also mentioned it in this issue.
- [x] I have learned the Github Markdown syntax, and formatted my issue correctly.

I understand that my issue may be closed if I don't fulfill my promises.

# Request

It would be nice to have an auto-linking of functions used as inline and block code, similar to what {pkgdown} does.

Luckily, @krlmlr found out that one can simply do

```r
    files <- dir("bookdown/_book/", pattern = "[.]html$", full.names = TRUE)
    purrr::walk(files, ~ {
      print(system.time(pkgdown::autolink_html(.x)))
    })
```

to get {pkgdown}-like auto-linking of R code functions.
(This is of course just an example and could be replaced by code with less/zero dependencies.)

Some details to this:
- If there is a {pkgdown} site available for pkg::fun, the link will point to the reference page of the {pkgdown} site
- Otherwise, the link will point to rdocumentation.org

Right now, we achieve this by running the code above during the CI run.
However, I think it would be nice to have this available as a built-in functionality for the `gitbook` format.
Maybe even with a toggable flag somewhere.

# Example

Have a look at the first instance of `data.table()` in https://mlr3book.mlr-org.com/tasks.html.

(Others are also auto-linked but using a non-convenient hack from our side).

I have built a few publicly available books in the past few days, and I have seen this bug multiple times.

To reproduce this one, download the R4DS book and try to build it. Make sure you do not have the **leaflet** package installed.

title: multi-line footnotes don't render in HTML version
description:
I ran into this issue with @cderv [over on the Rstudio](https://community.rstudio.com/t/multi-paragraph-footnotes/47076) community site, and he suggested that I should open an issue here. 

If you try to use a pandoc-style multi-line footnote (as shown below) it will not be rendered in the HTML version of the book, and following footnotes in the same chapter will be mis-numbered. (It will render correctly in the PDF and ePub file, though.)

If you add an empty page at the end of your book for citations, then the footnote will incorrectly show up there (unless there are additional footnotes after it in the same chapter, in which case it won't show up anywhere, even in the references/citations page). 

Sample footnote (number 1) that will not show up anywhere, even if you include a references/citations section:
```
Here is some text with a footnote[^1] specified.

Here's another paragraph[^2] with a second footnote[^3].


[^1]: This is my multi-paragraph footnote first paragraph.

    This is a continuation of the footnote.

[^2]: Second footnote text.

[^3]: Third footnote. 
``` 

I'm running the latest code and I've done my best to provide all the necessary information, including reproducible code. But I don't know what an "xfun::session_info('bookdown')" is. Nor have I tested this on the development version. Perhaps @cderv can help me out with those?

title: An request for an option to keep the `_files`
description:
Could there be an option to keep the build-up files for a `bookdown::word_document2`? 

I noticed that the `bookdown` used to create `_files` to keep plot files in a `*._files` folder (pdf for Latex and png for Word). I learned from Yihui's response [here](https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/issues/1553#issuecomment-482770550) that the program was designed to do so. I'm not sure since which version, this is no longer the case for the Word output. The `_files` fold will be automatically removed after the .docx file is built. Nevertheless, it could be helpful in some cases if these files could be maintained. For instance, many academic journals (at least in my area) require separate files of figures for publication. I used to send them the files in the `_files`, but now I have to manually save the plots from the output file or add saving codes everytime building up a plot in the rmd file.

Here's an illustrative example:

---

title: link-citations cannot be applied separately for different output formats
description:
I have confirmed that `link-citations` option cannot be applied separately for different output formats.

Let's say I want to set it to `true` for `bookdown::gitbook` output; but `false` for `bookdown::word_document2`.

So I did the following:

\_output.yml

```yaml
bookdown::gitbook:
  link-citations: true
bookdown::word_document2:
  link-citations: false
```

However, it does not work, which means citations are not linked in both outputs.

I have even tried with the following syntax:

\_output.yml

```yaml
bookdown::gitbook:
  pandoc_args: --metadata link-citations=true
bookdown::word_document2:
  pandoc_args: --metadata link-citations=false
```

This time; however, `--metadata link-citations` flag is interpreted as an unknown option.

I have used `pandoc` v2.8.1, the latest version as of this writing.

title: `serve_book()` doesn't refresh correctly when Rmd file in subdir changes
description:

title: Bug: Figure caption counting keeps being appended to previous chapter when appendix_name is customized
description:
This is another bug that I have just found.

When `appendix_name` field has been customized in `bookdown.yml`, any figures included in Appendix section is captioned appended to your previous chapter.

For example, let's say you have three chapters and the last figure before your appendix is captioned as "Figure 3.11:", then the following setup will give you your figure in `Appendix A` as "Figure 3.12:" instead of "Figure A.1:"

``` yaml
language:
  ui:
    appendix_name: "Appendix "
```

Please note that this bug does not occur when you do not customize `appendix_name` field.

title: Cannot customize Appendix prefix using a user-defined function
description:
Thanks for the recent change through #783; however, I found an issue.

I wanted to make my Appendix format such as `Appendix A: Title`, `Appendix A.1: Title`, `Appendix B: Title` ...

Thus, I added the following line in _bookdown.yml:

``` yaml
language:
  ui:
    appendix_name: !expr function(i) {paste0('Appendix ', i, ':', ' ')}
```

However, when I render the book using `bookdown::render_book("index.Rmd", output_format = "bookdown::gitbook")`, it throws the following error:

> Error in prefix != "" :                                                                                                                                
> comparison (2) is possible only for atomic and list types                                                                                            
> Calls: <Anonymous> ... split_chapters -> restore_appendix_html -> number_appendix                                                                      

FYI, there's no issue with the same syntax for `chapter_name` field when tested.

title: `clean_book()` not behaving as expected
description:
From my understanding the function `clean_book()` is designed to clean up after a book has been built. In the MWE provided below the suggested files/dirs to clean returned from `clean_book()` is solely the `_book/` dir which would actually be the one new directory I would want to keep - as it stores the rendered book. 

What am I missing?

In my MWE I am working in a directory with a dummy `index.Rmd` and one dummy chapter `.Rmd` - can provide if requested.
```r
library(bookdown)

original_files <- list.files()

# Don't clean the intermediate files, and don't remove objects in the
# global environment!
book <- render_book("index.Rmd", epub_book(), quiet = TRUE,
                    clean = FALSE, clean_envir = FALSE)

# capture newly created files
new_files <- setdiff(list.files(), original_files)

# `clean = FALSE` means the files to be deleted are listed, but not removed
to_clean <- clean_book(clean = FALSE)

# Expect to keep the folder with the book which we've just created (_book/), but
# we should get rid of everything else...
testthat::expect_equal(to_clean, setdiff(new_files, "_book"))

# FAILING! Intermediate files are not cleaned

# Tidy up after ourselves
unlink(new_files, recursive = TRUE)
```

title: Chapter title containing accents does not unfold sections in ToC
description:
<!--
Please keep the below portion in your issue. Your issue will be closed if any of the boxes is not checked (i.e., replace `[ ]` by `[x]`). In certain (rare) cases, you may be exempted if you give a brief explanation (e.g., you are only making a suggestion for improvement). Thanks!

Hello.

It is easy to reproduce this bug. Start with the *bookdown-demo* template. Then, create a new chapter including an accent in any of the words in the chapter title (for instance, if you write in Spanish, French, etc.). Include 2 section headers in the new chapter, for testing purposes.

```
# Título de capítulo

## Entrada uno

## Entrada dos
```
Use in `_output.yml` the following options to keep chapters folded in ToC at first load:

```
bookdown::gitbook:
  config:
    toc:
      collapse: section
      ... (rest of options)
```

Testing the ToC on the built website, when you click on the chapter entry in the ToC  the link is not hightlighted and the list of sections does not unfold. I think the link gets broken, somehow (not for rendering the chapter on the main section, but for the ToC highlighting functionality.

BTW, I have just checked that, even if the chapter title contains accents, if you add a specific link like in the example below, everything works again (list of sections unfolds, chapter name keeps highlighted, etc.):

```
# Título de capítulo con acentos {#mi-titulo}
```
It will not affect most users writing in English, but is quite annoying for users in other languages with accents (I have spent several hours with this bug, until I figured out what was going on).

title: Inclusion of external Rmd-file with latex equation environment leads to different PPTX output for rmarkdown and bookdow
description:
Below is the simplest Rmd file which I'm knitting to MS PowerPoint presentation using latest RStudio and latest bookdown:


    ---
    output:
      powerpoint_presentation: default
      bookdown::powerpoint_presentation2: default
    ---
    
    ```{sh, echo=FALSE, comment=''}
    cat ~/latex-test.Rmd
    ```


The contents of `~/latex-test.Rmd` are as follows:

```
Auto-numbered equation:

$$ f(x) = \sin(x) $$ 

---

LaTeX equation without label (using `\begin{equation}...\end{equation}`)

\begin{equation}
h(z) = \sinh(z)
\end{equation}

---

LaTeX equation with bookdown-supported label (using `\begin{equation}...(\#eq:label)\end{equation}`)

\begin{equation}
  f\left(k\right) = \binom{n}{k} p^k\left(1-p\right)^{n-k}
  (\#eq:binom)
\end{equation}

---

LaTeX equation with Xaringan-supported label (using `\begin{equation}...\label{label}\end{equation}`):

\begin{equation}
  g\left(k\right) = \binom{n}{k} p^k\left(1-p\right)^{n-k}
\label{binom2}
\end{equation}
```

Knitting to `powerpoint_presentation: default` gives exactly the same contents of PPTX file as contained in `~/latex-test.Rmd`.  
So I will not include it here to save the space.

But knitting to `bookdown::powerpoint_presentation2: default` gives extra `$$...$$` which surround `equation` environments:

title: Feature request: option for "view on GitHub" button on gitbook toolbar
description:
It would be great to have a button similar to "edit" that allows the reader to *view* the file on GitHub. When I'm reading bookdown books, 95% of the time I just want to see the source code, not edit it. I still click on the edit button but it takes a few additional clicks to see the file without having to fork the repository. Also, some people may be intimidated to click "edit" just to see the source code, so they would benefit from a separate button as well.

I realize I can change the behavior of the edit button to do what I want by changing the `edit:` link in `_bookdown.yml`, but don't want to do that in order to maintain consistency of buttons across all bookdown books.

title: Unable to compile with nostarch.cls, possibly because of \MakeUppercase
description:
By filing an issue to this repo, I promise that

- [x] I have fully read the issue guide at https://yihui.name/issue/.
- [x] I have provided the necessary information about my issue.
    - Since my example requires several files, I have put it in a GitHub repo at <https://github.com/gvwilson/bookdown-nostarch/>. The `README.md` file contains detailed information to supplement the bug report below.
- [x] I have learned the Github Markdown syntax, and formatted my issue correctly.

1.  I am attempting to use Bookdown with the style files provided by [No Starch Press](https://nostarch.com/).
2.  After installing TinyTex on my Mac, and then installing packages one by one as LaTeX complains, I am able to compile the example provided by No Starch.
3.  When I attempt to compile a small example using Bookdown, I get an error.
4.  The error appears to be related to the formatting of bibliographic citations: if I remove one line from `index.Rmd` that includes an `@tag` citation, the example compiles, but it fails with that line.
5.  The command-line output from Bookdown shows that compilation is getting as far as `pandoc`, and then `tlmgr` is trying to find a missing file `/tikzlibrarytopaths.code.tex`. It attempts to reinstall `pgf` to resolve the issue, but `pgf` is already present and compilation fails.
6.  The final error message complains about an undefined control sequence `\MakeUppercase ...ppercaseUnsupportedInPdfStrings` (the ellipsis `...` is present in the error message).
7.  `grep` shows that `\MakeUppercase` is used in `nostarch.cls`, but is not defined there; online searches tell me that `\MakeUppercase` is defined by standard LaTeX packages.
8.. If I include a bibliographic citation in the No Starch example `\cite{...}`, it compiles without error.

I therefore believe that something in Bookdown is undefined `\MakeUppercase` or blocking the loading of a file that would define it. Please see <https://github.com/gvwilson/bookdown-nostarch/> for a minimal working example and further documentation.

title: Suggestion for improvement: selectable babel for non-pdflatex
description:
If my understanding is correct, it is hard-coded in `bookdown` that selecting `pdftex` selects `babel`, while `xetex` and `luatex` selects `polyglossia`.

However, `polyglossia` right now is not really useful for languages like Hungarian, as even fundamental typesetting guidelines are not yet implemented (see [here](https://github.com/reutenauer/polyglossia/issues/344)) as opposed to `babel`. As [it seems](https://tex.stackexchange.com/a/482401/8064) other people have similar considerations, may I suggest a change to somehow (header option?) make the multilanguage-solution selectable, irrespectively of what LaTeX engine you use?

This follows on from [my StackOverflow question](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/58164239/compile-bookdown-to-markdown).

What is the best way to build Bookdown project with **Markdown** instead of HTML or TeX?

I ask because I need to post-process the final Markdown output from Bookdown, in order to extract R and Python notebooks for download.

In more detail, I am using Bookdown to build a textbook that embeds notebooks to download, where the notebooks contain subsets of the code and text in the bookdown `.Rmd` files.  For example, a single chapter could contain more than one notebook.

In order to do this, I put start and end comment markers in the RMarkdown input text to identify the section that will be a notebook, and then post-process the generated Markdown files to extract the notebook section.  As in something like:

~~~
<!--- notebook: first_section.Rmd
-->

Some explanation, maybe using Bookdown extra markup such as @a_citation.

```{r}
a <- 1
a
```

<!--- end of notebook
-->

More markdown.

```{r}
# More code not in notebook.
b <- 2
```
~~~

Obviously I could use the input RMarkdown pages, but this would be ugly, because all the extended Bookdown markup such as citations, cross-references and so on, would appear in raw and ugly form in the generated notebook.  So I'd really like to be able to get the final output Markdown, after merging, resolving of citations and cross references.  Is there any way of doing that?

I have tried setting `clean=FALSE` in the `bookdown::render_book` call, but this resulted in intermediate Markdown files for each chapter, with citations and `(ref:foo)` style references not resolved.  These intermediate files appear identical to the `.md` files already written to the output directory in my Knit / Merge build.

I have also tried `output_format='rmarkdown::md_document'` - but this appears to result in an output document `_main.md`, which is then deleted during the build.

I was considering looking into making my own output format - is that the right way to go?  Or is there another way of doing this?

I have asked [this question on StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/57737225/programmatic-way-to-get-output-directory-in-bookdown), and waited a week or so, but got no response.

Is there a way to detect the Bookdown output directory in code running within an RMarkdown document?

## Summary

I want to be able to get the bookdown output directory, from inline R code, running during the Bookdown build.

### Why?

I am writing a book that uses Python code.   I want to build Jupyter Notebooks from the `.Rmd` page, for some pages, for the user to download and run.   I am imagining an effect like the one you see at the top of [this page](https://matthew-brett.github.io/dsfe/chapters/01/Plotting_the_Classics), where you can click on a "Download" or "Interact" link at the top of the page, to get the Jupyter version.

To create that effect, I wanted to put something like this at top of the relevant `.Rmd` files:

```
`r make_link_notebook()`
```

where the `make_link_notebook` function creates the Jupyter Notebook file, and makes a link to the notebook within the output document.

To do this, `make_link_notebook` needs to know where the Bookdown output directory is, in order to copy the notebook file.  

By default, of course, this is `_book`, but I am customizing the output directory in some configuration files, so I want to be able to find the output directory programmatically.

I have tried investigating Knitr's `root.dir` option, but of course this points to the directory containing the source document. 

Is there any programmatic way my R code can work out the directory to which the output will be written?

Thanks much for any help.

title: Feature request: Support for code folding buttons
description:
Hi,

I recently searched for an option to have buttons that hide the R code output since it was not supported via a simple option in `bookdown::gitbook`. Using [this stackoverflow answer](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/45360998/code-folding-in-bookdown) I implemented somewhat of a hacked version with nice CSS (from the `united` bootstrap theme) for the buttons and it looks like [this](https://bblodfon.github.io/gitsbe-model-analysis/atopo/cell-lines-2500/a498-model-analysis.html). For the individual R chunks the solution is nice, though for the **hide-show-all** button that is in the right-up corner, the solution is sowewhat (!) hacked (`position: fixed` in the CSS). But it works so it's good enough for me :)

I was considering though that it would be really nice, to have the option integrated globally in gitbook, where the **hide-show-all** button would be in the toolbar (like all the other sharing buttons - github, fb, etc.) and the config would look somewhat like this:

```
bookdown::gitbook:
  config:
    show_codefolding_buttons: true # to show all the buttons
    hide_code: true # initial configuration, no R code is shown if above is true
```

BR, John.
