title: image in `toc: before:` field is not copied to output directory
description:
Hi, 

@apreshill and I have found that image files (like a logo) included the `before:` field of `_output.yml` are not being copied over to the output directory. 

Reproducible example [here](https://github.com/dcossyleon/book-with-logo/tree/master).

We know how to force it to work (e.g. including the image elsewhere in the book), but it seems like the problem is an unexpected behavior based on the [description](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/rmarkdown/versions/1.14/topics/find_external_resources) of where `rmarkdown` looks for resources. 

We have also tried including this in the YAML of `index.Rmd`:
```
resource_files: logo.png
```

Is there a way to "declare" an image resource for an image that is not used in any other book chapters? 

I'm asking because we're developing an RStudio project template for others to use, and we're trying to provide the most minimal features needed to get a logo image working.

title: Would you mind developing word_book() output format?
description:
I was wondering if there would be any way that someone could develop `bookdown::word_book()` output format just like either `bookdown::pdf_book()` or `bookdown::html_book()`.

It would be so much appreciated if `word_book()` format could be implemented.
Many thanks!

title: Problematic assessment of CSL/pandoc-citeproc in the docs
description:
I feel the opening passages in <https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/citations.html> do not do justice to CSL in general, and pandoc-citeproc in particular.

> Although Pandoc supports multiple ways of writing citations, we recommend you to use BibTeX databases because they work best with LaTeX/PDF output.

To my mind, this is not a fair assessment. Neither are BibTeX databases inherently “better”, nor do BibTeX or biber/BibLaTeX (the programs) necessarily do a better job processing these than pandoc-citeproc does. Sure, pandoc-citeproc has to convert BibTeX or BibLaTeX data to CSL-JSON first, but it takes great care to make this process as lossless as possible. On the other hand, if bibliographic data are already available in the CSL-JSON format (e.g., from Zotero, or similar CSL-based reference managers), there is no reason at all to convert these to BibTeX when using pandoc-citeproc.

Also, I would argue that BibTeX (the program) itself is pretty much obsolete, and its data model severely limited by modern standards. (Even <https://www.ctan.org/pkg/bibtex> concedes that its “facilities rapidly run out as one moves away from simple ASCII […] For more flexibility, the user is urged to consider using biber with BibLaTeX […]“)

BibTeX’s more modern successor, BibLaTeX, arguably is on a par with CSL/pandoc-citeproc in terms of their data models and processing capabilities, at least as far as the average user wishing or needing to follow a particular style guide is concerned. (I’ll readily admit that BibLaTeX allows a lot more fine-tuning, provided one has mastered that particular art. However, BibLaTeX/BibTeX is limited to one single output format, PDF, whereas no such limitations exist for CSL/pandoc-citeproc. In addition, CSL provides far more well-maintained styles implementing the recommendations of recognised style guides, including popular ones, such as Chicago, APA, MLA, etc., and more niche variants for specific journals or university departments than BibLaTeX does.)

> Pandoc can process other types of bibliography databases with the utility pandoc-citeproc (https://github.com/jgm/pandoc-citeproc), but it may not render certain bibliography items correctly (especially in case of multiple authors per item).

I’d kindly ask to see the evidence for this rather sweeping claim.

As to “especially in case of multiple authors per item” -- if this is based on the perception that pandoc(-citeproc)’s output where “The first author is displayed in the format Lastname, Firstname, but the rest of authors are displayed in Firstname Lastname“ (see <https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/issues/703#issuecomment-490521437>) is somehow incorrect, I’d like to point out that this is *exactly* what the *Chicago Manual of Style* calls for.

I’d be happy if the passages in question could be reworded in order not to needlessly discourage users from working with CSL/pandoc-citeproc.

Everyone should of course feel free to report any genuine issues concerning CSL and/or pandoc-citeproc at either <https://forums.zotero.org/discussions> (for CSL style file issues) or at <https://github.com/jgm/pandoc-citeproc/issues> (for pandoc-citeproc).

title: Enhancement: option to disable bookdown extension
description:
It would be useful to have the option to disable bookdown extension. 
Or to change where there are injected in the template.

Here is a use case. One basic markdown, one basic preamble.tex

````
---
title: Theorem test
author: jm
output:
  bookdown::pdf_book:
    includes:
      in_header: preamble.tex
    keep_tex: yes
  bookdown::gitbook: default  
---

# Hello world

Normal text

```{theorem, name="Pythagorean theorem"}
For a right triangle, if $c$ denotes the length of the hypotenuse
and $a$ and $b$ denote the lengths of the other two sides, we have
$$a^2 + b^2 = c^2$$
```

Normal text
````

```
% Start of preamble

\newenvironment{FOO}{}

% of of preamble
```


The generated tex file contains the following:

```
% Start of preamble

\newenvironment{FOO}{}

% of of preamble

\usepackage{amsthm}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[section]
\newtheorem{lemma}{Lemma}[section]
\newtheorem{corollary}{Corollary}[section]
\newtheorem{proposition}{Proposition}[section]
\newtheorem{conjecture}{Conjecture}[section]
\theoremstyle{definition}
\newtheorem{definition}{Definition}[section]
\theoremstyle{definition}
\newtheorem{example}{Example}[section]
\theoremstyle{definition}

\newtheorem*{remark}{Remark}

\let\BeginKnitrBlock\begin \let\EndKnitrBlock\end
\begin{document}
\maketitle
```

Looking at the template, the insertion before the begin{document} is not defined there. My search leads to Latex.R file. I do not understand properly what is happening there.

The issue is that one user cannot define theorems using any of these names in the preamble. The current workaround would be to define them in the include before body.

title: The compile order of the Rmd files in subdirectories
description:
**Behavior:** 

When I specify the `rmd_subdir` metadata in the `_bookdown.yml`, I would expect the all Rmd files be compiled in order.  However, it compiles the files according to alphabetic order of the name of sub-directories. 

**minimal reproducible example:**

Start a default bookdown project using Rstudio.
Assume the directory structure is like the following.

```
.... (some necessary files)
- index.Rmd
- part1
   -- 01-pre.Rmd (Remark: In this file, I only created a one-line content `# Part I: foo {-}`)
   -- 02-foo.Rmd
   -- 03-bar.Rmd
- appendix
   -- 01-appendix-pre.Rmd (Remark: In this file, I only created a one-line content `# Part II: foo {-}`)
   -- 02-appendix-a.Rmd
   -- 03-appendix-b.Rmd
```
And I specify the `red_subdir` like this.

```
rmd_subdir: ['part1/','appendix/']
```

According to [guide](https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/usage.html) in the usage of `rmd_files`, I expect the all Rmd files in the subdir `part1` would be compiled first. But it turns out that the `appendix` is compiled first. So the final order is like

```
01-appendix-pre.Rmd
02-appendix-a.Rmd
03-appendix-b.Rmd
01-pre.Rmd
02-foo.Rmd
03-bar.Rmd
```

My current workaround is to name the subdirectories like `0part1` and `1appendix`. Then each file is rendered in desired order.

title: Margin/div bug when rendering gitbook
description:
I have encountered a problem with rendering a book in the gitbook format (`bookdown::render_book('file.Rmd')`). title: header-include, include-before, and include-after variables to be passed to Pandoc default template are lost
description:
In [Section D.8 The default HTML template](https://bookdown.org/yihui/blogdown/default-template.html) of _Creating Websites with R Markdown_, all of `$header-includes$`, `$css$`, `$include-before$`, `$toc$`, and `$include-after$` are supposed to be available for customization of the Pandoc output of R Markdown posts, but only `$css$` and `$toc$` appear to work. Any values passed to the  `$header-includes$`, `$include-before$`, and `$include-after$` variables disappear without an error message.

## Steps to reproduce:

1. In RStudio, select File > New Project...
2. Select New Directory.
3. Select Website using blogdown.
4. Provide a directory name, use the default yihui/hugo-lithium Hugo theme, leave Add sample blog posts, Add the example site of the theme, and Convert all metadata to YAML checked, and then create project.
5. Addins > Serve Site
6. Open the file content/post/2015-07-23-r-markdown.html in the editor, confirm it has been rendered, and close the editor pane.
7. Open the file content/post/2015-07-23-r-markdown.Rmd in the editor. Add the below to the front matter of the file and save it: 
```
output:
  blogdown::html_page:
    toc: true
    css: "/css/my-style.css"
```
8. Open content/post/2015-07-23-r-markdown.html in the editor again, confirm a CSS tag and table of contents have been added, and close the editor pane.
9. In content/post/2015-07-23-r-markdown.Rmd, add the below options to `blogdown::html_page:` in the front matter:
```
    header-includes: "This is a header include."
    include-before: "This is a before include."
    include-after: "This is an after include."
```
10. Open content/post/2015-07-23-r-markdown.html in the editor again and confirm none of these were included.
11. In content/post/2015-07-23-r-markdown.Rmd, change the options to `blogdown::html_page:` in the front matter to be arrays, as in the below:
```
    header-includes: ["This is a header include.", "This is another example include."]
    include-before: ["This is a before include.", "This is another example include."]
    include-after: ["This is an after include.", "This is another example include."]
```
12. Open content/post/2015-07-23-r-markdown.html in the editor again and confirm there are still no inclusions.

This is what the final front matter looks like for content/post/2015-07-23-r-markdown.Rmd:
```
---
title: "Hello R Markdown"
author: "Frida Gomam"
date: 2015-07-23T21:13:14-05:00
categories: ["R"]
tags: ["R Markdown", "plot", "regression"]
output:

    toc: true
    css: "/css/my-style.css"

    include-before: ["This is a before include.", "This is another example include."]

---

I have posted this issue some time ago on stackoverflow, but had no answers:
[https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55865129/how-can-i-generate-footnote-url-links-with-an-r-function-in-bookdown-knitr-doc](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55865129/how-can-i-generate-footnote-url-links-with-an-r-function-in-bookdown-knitr-doc)

**Original stackoverflow post**
I try to generate URL links through an R-function. These links are inteded to be included in footnotes primarily.

I generate the links in text references, and this works nicely in html output. In PDF (latex) though, it does not. In the document, I only see the empty (ref:some-text-ref) lines.

I work in RStudio, all packages are up to date.

I looked at https://stackoverflow.com/questions/49990699/bookdown-add-url-as-footnote. The proposes solution with redefining href is not satisfactory since I still want to be able to use href in a non-footnote context. Also, the problem here seems to be somewhere else because the links are not included in either html or pdf output.



The following code demonstrates the problem.

````
---
author: "Author"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
title: Testing footnotes
site: bookdown::bookdown_site
link-citations: yes
toc-depth: 2
always_allow_html: yes
output:
  bookdown::pdf_book:
      template: null
      latex_engine: xelatex
      keep_tex: yes
      highlight: pygments
  bookdown::gitbook:
      lib_dir: assets
      css: style.css
      split_by: section
      highlight: pygments
---

```{r linker, include=FALSE, results='hide'}
library(stringr)

github_base_url = "https://github.com/user/repo/tree/master"

make_github_link <- function(..., text = ""){
  subdirs <- list(...)
  
  if (length(subdirs) == 0) {
    directory = ""
  } else {
    directory = paste(...,sep="/")
  }
  url = paste(github_base_url, directory, sep="/")
  
  if (text == ""){
    base = str_match(github_base_url, "(https://)([a-z/.-].*)(tree/master)")[3]
    link_text = paste0(base, directory)
  } else {
    link_text = text
  }
  sprintf("[%s](%s)", link_text, url)
}

```

```{r setup_knitr, include=F, results='hide'}

inline_hook <- function (x) {
  if (is.numeric(x)) {
    res <- ifelse(x == round(x),
      sprintf("%d", x),
      sprintf("%.3f", x)
    )
    paste(res, collapse = ", ")
  }
}

title: Syntax highlighting for Stata
description:
Dear all, 

I need to highlight Stata syntax in gitbook using bookdown. I learned [here](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#syntax-highlighting) that Pandoc uses the [skylighting](https://github.com/jgm/skylighting) for highlighting, but when I execute `pandoc --list-highlight-languages`, Stata is not listed as one of the languages supported. However, given that gitbook is html, I was wondering whether it is possible to either add Stata syntax in skylighting, which I already asked [here](https://github.com/jgm/skylighting/issues/74), or change the syntax highlighiting from skylighting to [highlight.js](http://highlightjs.org). I was able to highlight Stata syntax using *blogdown*, but I have not idea how to do it in bookdown. 

I also asked the same question in [stackoverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/56049586/stata-syntax-highlighting-in-rmarkdown) almost three weeks ago, but I have not got any answer yet. 

My question is simple, how can I add Stata syntax highlighting to a gitbook created with Bookdown?

I highly appreciate your help. 

Best, 
Andres

title: Special character does not show up in bibliography (but works in body)
description:
Hi,

NB: I have asked [a question on SO](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55342838/special-character-does-not-show-up-in-bibliography-but-works-in-body-in-bookdo) that remained unanswered so I'm opening an issue here.

I am writing my dissertation with `bookdown` and the `memoir` class in `R`. I need to include special characters such as "\oe". This character appears correctly in the body of the document (therefore it's NOT a font problem).

However, the same character does not appear in the bibliography section. More precisely, nothing appears instead of the special character. The .bib file is a .tex generated by Zotero where the "\oe" symbol (for instance) is represented as "Å".

I have disabled citation packages in order to format the bibliography section following a specific citation style (i.e., I am using the apa6.csl), so the problem might come from there. However, I am also regularly writing articles in RMarkdown using this same csl file (and using the [`papaja` package](https://github.com/crsh/papaja)) and this never happened before, so it seems to be specific to `bookdown`...

It is difficult to provide a reproducible example though, as I am working from my messy dissertation repository. But here is (a part of) my `_output.yml `file:

```
bookdown::pdf_book:
  includes:
    in_header: latex/preamble.tex # defines style and latex options
    before_body: latex/before_body.tex # defines cover page
  latex_engine: xelatex # lualatex or xelatex
  citation_package: none # needs to be "none" in order to use the csl file
  keep_tex: true # keeps the .tex file
  dev: "cairo_pdf"
  toc: false # deactivates default table of contents
  highlight: pygments # code highlighting
  pandoc_args: [ "--csl", "./csl/apa6.csl" ] # specifies the csl file to be used
```

Any idea ?

title: links in blocks don't have footnotes in pdf
description:
Hi there,

I recently started with `bookdown` and it looks great!

I have been using a few custom blocks and it works well in general. However, I found out that in linked text within the blocks doesn't get properly converted into footnotes when building the pdf. The linked text gets the proper numbered superscript, but the footnote is not printed anywhere. This happens with both `block` and `block2`.

The footnotes are created without problem outside the custom blocks.

So, this generates the appropriate footnote
```rmarkdown
This is an [link](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown)
```
But this doesn't
```rmarkdown
    ```{block2 type="rmdnote"}
    This is an [link](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown)
    ```
```

I guess this has something to do with the `preamble.tex` code or the way the custom blocks are implemented. I tried fiddling with the `preamble.tex`, but after few attempts I got nothing (I'm not very familiar with Latex).

Initial test was with bookdown 0.8 but the issue persists in 0.10.

R version 3.5.1 (2018-07-02)
Platform: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu (64-bit)
Running under: Ubuntu 16.04.6 LTS

Cheers,
Xabi

description:

I'm trying to reproduce, which is a bit hard due to different nature from when using Rscript vs. using RStudio.  

## Problem

LaTeX failures when `rlang`-style traceback in PDF book in `bookdown`, when `error = TRUE` in code chunk.

This may be due to @r-lib `rlang` not recognizing PDF output (not sure if it should) or `bookdown` should set option if necessary.

## Solution

Set `options(rlang_backtrace_on_error = "none")` in `Rmd` file.

## Example failures

### With `xelatex`

```
/usr/local/bin/pandoc +RTS -K512m -RTS test.utf8.md --to latex --from markdown+autolink_bare_uris+ascii_identifiers+tex_math_single_backslash --output test.tex --table-of-contents --toc-depth 2 --template /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.5/Resources/library/rmarkdown/rmd/latex/default-1.17.0.2.tex --number-sections --highlight-style tango --pdf-engine xelatex --natbib --variable graphics=yes --wrap preserve --variable 'geometry:margin=1in' --variable 'compact-title:yes' --variable tables=yes --standalone 
This is XeTeX, Version 3.14159265-2.6-0.99998 (TeX Live 2017) (preloaded format=xelatex)
 restricted \write18 enabled.
entering extended mode
! Text line contains an invalid character.
l.191 ^^[
         [90m  1. ^^[[39mbookdown::render_book(input = ".", output_format = ...

Error: Failed to compile test.tex. See https://yihui.name/tinytex/r/#debugging for debugging tips. See test.log for more info.
```

## With `pdflatex`:

```
! Package inputenc Error: Keyboard character used is undefined
(inputenc)                in inputencoding `utf8'.
```


## Does not reproduce in `reprex`

I think this may be due to traceback options in `rlang` with non-UTF8 characters in traceback for PDF outputs for `bookdown.

Here is the uploaded test files:
[test.zip](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/files/3132337/test.zip), but they are downloaded in the scrip below.


I have not found this to completely reproduce in @tidyverse reprex, but if you run this script locally (RStudio or Terminal R), it will error whenever `rlang_backtrace_on_error` seems to be set to anything but `"none"` or `"reminder"':



``` r
options(tinytex.verbose = TRUE); 
destfile = tempfile(fileext = ".zip")
download.file("https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/files/3132337/test.zip",
              destfile = destfile)
outdir = tempfile()
dir.create(outdir, recursive = TRUE)
unz = unzip(zipfile = destfile, exdir = outdir)

test_dir = file.path(outdir, "test")
dir(test_dir)
dir.exists(test_dir)
setwd(test_dir)

#' ## pdflatex with no branching - works
options(rlang_backtrace_on_error = "none")
bookdown::render_book(input = ".", output_format = "bookdown::pdf_book",
                      output_options=list(latex_engine = "pdflatex"))

#' ## pdflatex with reminder only - works
options(rlang_backtrace_on_error = "reminder")
bookdown::render_book(input = ".", output_format = "bookdown::pdf_book",
                      output_options=list(latex_engine = "pdflatex"))


#' ## pdflatex with branching - fails
options(rlang_backtrace_on_error = "branch")
bookdown::render_book(input = ".", output_format = "bookdown::pdf_book",
                      output_options=list(latex_engine = "pdflatex"))

#' ## xelatex with no branching - works
options(rlang_backtrace_on_error = "none")
bookdown::render_book(input = ".", output_format = "bookdown::pdf_book",
                      output_options=list(latex_engine = "xelatex"))
#' ## xelatex with branching - fails
options(rlang_backtrace_on_error = "branch")
bookdown::render_book(input = ".", output_format = "bookdown::pdf_book",
                      output_options=list(latex_engine = "xelatex"))
```

title: bookdown TOC page number mismatch with content
description:
I use bookdown to create a tech report by having an existing cover page (cover.pdf) and a "copyright" page using child '.rmd' right after cover page.  Somehow, the page number from the TOC is 1 page less than the actual page number in the content (i.e., 6 in the TOC, but it's 7 in the page).

Since I want the cover page and copyright page shown prior to the TOC. Here is what I did.

1. define before_body.txt in the YAML and set toc: FALSE.
----------------------------------------------

toc: FALSE   # use Latex to trigger TOC later
 includes:
            before_body: before_body.tex
            in_header: preamble.tex 
----------------------------------------------

2. Include cover.pdf in the before_body.text
---------------------------------------------
\thispagestyle{empty}
\begin{center}
\includegraphics{cover.pdf}
\end{center}
-----------------------------------------------
3.  Use child to produce 'copyright' page and latex to trigger TOC.
----------------------------------------------
```{r copyright, child = "copyright.Rmd"}
```

```{=latex}
% Trigger ToC creation in LaTeX
\tableofcontents
\pagebreak

\listoftables
\pagebreak

\listoffigures
\pagebreak

```
-----------------------------------------------
Does anyone know why?

title: keybindings should be discoverable
description:
Keyboard shortcuts are not discoverable by users. The ones I have uncovered:

* `f` opens the search input with an active cursor
* `<left>` and `<right>` navigate to the head of the next/previous chapter
* `<up>` and `<down>` navigate to the next/previous search match (assuming search is active)

I don't know the best way to educate users. Sites like GitHub and GMail offer a `?` shortcut, but then there is the issue of having users discover _that_ shortcut.

Things like `f` are documented in the bookdown book, but that is educating the book _authors_, not the readers. https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/html.html#gitbook-style

Features in the bookdown GitBook style should be more self-discoverable by the reader. We should not leave it to each book author to create that logic.

This issue appears to be present in bookdown 0.1 to 0.9. The RStudio Connect Admin Guide is an example using a SHA close to 0.7.7 and does not appear to have discoverable keyboard shortcuts. https://docs.rstudio.com/connect/admin/

description: 1. Visit a bookdown-built book deployed to an HTTP server, such as: https://docs.rstudio.com/connect/admin/ 1. Use the 'f' keyboard shortcut to open the search input dialog. 1. title: search persists across page loads
description:
1. Visit a bookdown-built book deployed to an HTTP server, such as: https://docs.rstudio.com/connect/admin/
2. Use the 'f' keyboard shortcut to open the search input dialog.
3. Type in a search phrase; try "safari".
4. Now, visit another bookdown-built book deployed to the same HTTP server, such as:
https://docs.rstudio.com/ide/server-pro/
5. Observe that the search term "safari" is automatically active in this second book.

This appears to be a long-standing issue. The RStudio IDE Server Pro documentation was built with bookdown 0.1 (according to the HTML metadata). The RStudio Connect Admin Guide was built with a pinned git SHA close to bookdown 0.7.7. I am actively updating to bookdown 0.9 and still see search phrases persisting across page loads.

I understand why local storage is being used to maintain search phrases - different portions of a book may reside in different HTML and the search phrase needs to persist as matching chapters/sections are visited.

Scenarios to consider:
1. Multiple books hosted on the same domain. Search should not persist when following links between books.
2. Multiple tabs open against the same book. Search in one tab should not persist when a second tab is opened against the same book.
3. Revisiting a book after time has passed. Search should not persist when returning to that book at some later time.

All three of these scenarios persist search terms today in both the RSP and RStudio Connect documentation.

title: Figure & table preview by mouse hovering over \@ref() generated hyperlink
description:
Many thanks for the hard work you've put into this package, it is a real game-changer. 

**Feature request**: I'm not sure how feasible this is, but a great feature would be a "hover preview" of figures/tables when mouseovering/mouse hovering over a hyperlink generated by `\@ref(fig:link)` or `\@ref(tab:link)`. 

**Context**: In my bookdown project, I like to often refer back to previously seen figures/tables, both for context-building and repetition/practice. However, it is quite a time commitment to either:
1. scroll to the figure/table if it's on the same page
2. click on a hyperlink, see the previous figure/table, hit "back" on the browser, and wait for the browser to reset to the point in the page where the hyperlink is. 

Having a "hover preview" would speed things up nicely.

title: Provide `latex_extension` option when compling PDF
description:
In bookdown, basically, I want to preserve Chinese quotation marks in the PDF output. This is related to https://stackoverflow.com/questions/52052231/how-to-write-chinese-quotes-in-bookdown

The reason why adding `md_extensions: -smart` did not work is that in pandoc, `smart` extension is enabled for latex by default, no matter latex is the input or output.

```bash
pandoc --version
# pandoc 2.6
# Compiled with pandoc-types 1.17.5.4, texmath 0.11.2, skylighting 0.7.6
# Default user data directory: /home/hongyuanjia/.pandoc
# Copyright (C) 2006-2019 John MacFarlane
# Web:  http://pandoc.org
# This is free software; see the source for copying conditions.
# There is no warranty, not even for merchantability or fitness
# for a particular purpose.

pandoc --list-extensions=latex | grep "smart"
# +smart
```

So the only way to achieve this is to disable the `smart` extension both for markdown and latex.

```bash
echo "“”" | pandoc -f markdown-smart -t latex
# ``''

echo "“”" | pandoc -f markdown-smart -t latex-smart
# “”
```

However, in bookdown, the PDF is compiled using pandoc with only "-t latex", and there is no such `latex_extension` option to modify latex extension in pandoc.

title: when tidy=T & echo=F, pdf renders source code as if echo=T

description:
Hi

This is copy paste from my [unanswered SO post](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/54597176/format-of-formattableas-datatable-breaks-when-compiled-as-gitbook-with-bookdow). I just updated the package versions at the end.

I want to include a `ft <- formattable::formattable(...)` into a `gitbook` via `formattable::as.datatable(ft)`. However, `bookdown::render_book()` somehow breaks the format of that table.

I need the table as an `datatable` object since this enables the user to sort the table according to the values in the columns in the final html document. Furthermore, I would like to use the `formattable` features to visualize the values as bars in the background of the table elements from left to right. 

Please see this minimal example `index.Rmd`:

````
---
site: bookdown::bookdown_site
documentclass: book
output:

---

```{r echo=F}
df <- data.frame(type=letters[1:3], val=c(1, 0.007, 0.001))
library(formattable)
ft <- formattable::formattable(df, list(
            val=formattable::formatter("span",
                  style=function(x) {
                      formattable::style(display="inline-block",

                                "border-radius"="4px",
                                "background-color"="#b8dff3",
                                width=formattable::percent(x))

formattable::as.datatable(ft, options=list(dom='t'))

When I run the last line of this code, `formattable::as.datatable(ft, options=list(dom='t'))`, in the R terminal, the table looks exactly as I want it:

In the gitbook, which I compile via `bookdown::render_book("index.Rmd", "bookdown::gitbook")`, the table looks like this:

Somehow `render_book()` tries to fit the long character string `0.001` into the very short background bar of `formattable::formattable()`.

title: Equation numbering in docx should be improved and shown as PDF/LaTeX
description:
I have simple bookdown document with labeled LaTeX equation:

```
---
title: "Equation text"
output: 
  bookdown::pdf_document2: default
  bookdown::word_document2: default
---

Below is the binom equation

\begin{equation}
f\left(k\right)=\binom{n}{k}p^k\left(1-p\right)^{n-k} (\#eq:binom)
\end{equation}
```

With RStudio it Knits normally to PDF:

![PDF](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/309456/53683803-173d9f00-3d16-11e9-84f0-9513be66eddb.png)

and to docx:

![d](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/309456/53683809-26245180-3d16-11e9-9060-f91dbfc9755d.png)

But this docx-rendering is technically incorrect, as we have equation number inside OMML equation. And the number is separated from equation by `\qquad` or similar symbols (hex `E2 80 81 E2 80 81` in resulting docx between `<m:t>` and `</m:t>`).

The correct form for DOCX is expected to be as following:

![sds](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/309456/53683900-97183900-3d17-11e9-8184-4773bbaefc11.png)

Here we have 2 tab stops:
1. at the middle of the page for centering the equation 
2. at the right side of the page to place equation number.

Schematically it looks like:


```
              →                        EQ_centered             →                 (N)
```
```
             ^^^                           ^^^^^             ^^^                ^^^^
             Tab                       OMML object           Tab                text
```

The proposed behavior will make PDF/LaTeX and DOCX representations look consistent.
And it will fix my next problem with OMML to MathType conversion (see [my question on StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/q/54928343/937095).

As far I can understand this should be fixed on bookdown level.
Writing pandoc (Lua)filter and/or applying docx-template is harder to implement.

I'm using latest versions of bookdown, rmarkdown, pandoc and RStudio Preview.

title: Output-type specific top level YAML header options?
description:
I'm trying at [stackoverflow.com](https://stackoverflow.com/q/54868283/2103880) with zero takers, so I flock to the source ...
In the following YAML header example the `geometry` parameter is supposed to be used only when compiling to the `pdf_document2` target, as it's usage provokes a `LaTeX`-level option clash for the `pdf_book`/`beamer_presentation` target:

    ---

However, this does not work, as the `geometry` field appears in the `pandoc` produced `LaTeX` file also when set to any of `''` (as above), `NA`, `'NA'`, `NULL`, `'null'` and the option clash persists.

Is there any way to invoke top level YAML header options in a output-specific manner?

title: incompatibility with titlesec LaTeX package
description:
One fairly popular (and useful) package `titlesec` has incompatibility with `bookdown` since it adds this bit of tex:

```tex
% Redefines (sub)paragraphs to behave more like sections
\ifx\paragraph\undefined\else
\let\oldparagraph\paragraph
\renewcommand{\paragraph}[1]{\oldparagraph{#1}\mbox{}}
\fi
\ifx\subparagraph\undefined\else
\let\oldsubparagraph\subparagraph
\renewcommand{\subparagraph}[1]{\oldsubparagraph{#1}\mbox{}}
\fi
```
and this causes an error when the `titlesec` package is used:

```
! Argument of \paragraph has an extra }.
<inserted text> 
                \par 
l.1290 \ttl@extract\paragraph
```
A simple example is [in this repo](https://github.com/topepo/bookdown-demo-titlesec). 

I don't see any was around this as-is; the `tex` file would need to be edited prior to compiling the document.  If the paragraph stuff above is commented out, the `titlesec` changes work and I can't find any real difference in the book that I'm creating.

title: How to handle a specialized addition to bookdown?
description:
[This question](https://stackoverflow.com/q/54154890/2554330) on StackOverflow asks for a very specialized addition to `bookdown` to support the Hungarian language:  rather than `\ref` in LaTeX, it needs `\aref` from the `babel-magyar` package (or something like that), because Hungarian has special grammatical rules for dealing with numbers.

I wrote a [tiny package](https://github.com/dmurdoch/magyarbookdown) that monkey-patches bookdown when loaded to support `@aref` as well as `@ref`.  It's a pretty fragile solution, because as soon as `bookdown` updates one of the patched functions, my package will also need an update.  I could submit a PR to incorporate the code into the main `bookdown`, but I suspect there aren't really that many Hungarian users, and I doubt if the `bookdown` authors want to support this.  And there are a lot of languages, so there are probably other specialized patches that others would want.

So what would be a good strategy for going forward with this?

title: suggestions for a publishing process with two target formats
description:
We are in the final stages of writing our book using `bookdown`. We'll have both [HTML](https://bookdown.org/max/FES)  and LaTeX versions. 

Do you have any input on the sequence of events at the end of the cycle? The process that I see happening is:

 * Finalize `Rmd` files of main content
 * Build a "raw" pdf/LaTeX version to send for copyediting
 * Update the `Rmd` with copyediting changes.
 * Make a branch for the final LaTeX files. In that branch
   * Add `\index` commands
   * "Optimize" the LaTeX (e.g. figure positions, aesthetics, etc). 
   * Build the publisher's final version here

Is this the best sequence of events? 

My only thought about this is for a potential 2nd edition. We would have to re-do the indexing commands for a new version. Maybe a GH merge would make that happen cleanly but I doubt it. Keeping the custom LaTeX parts sequestered in a different branch is  probably a better approach than contaminating the `Rmd` files with LaTeX indexing bits and other nuances.

options("bookdown.post.latex" = function(x) {

title: Bibliography elements do not respect alphabetical order
description:
Bibliography elements in Bookdown (GitBook format) do not respect alphabetical order.

To reproduce the problem:

1. Open minimal bookdown example in RStudio.
2. Download [`apa.csl`](http://www.zotero.org/styles/apa) file and save it in project's folder.
3. In YAML header of `index.Rmd`, replace `biblio-style: apalike` with `csl: "apa.csl"`
4. At the end of `index.Rmd`, add citations in this order:
```md
1. [@xie2015]
2. [@R-rmarkdown]
3. [@R-knitr]
4. [@R-base]
5. [@R-bookdown]
```
5. Build a GitBook.

The result shows, that references are in the order as they were mentioned in the text:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12725868/49825662-a083ac00-fd8d-11e8-9e12-f6e4097888da.png)


If I use the same sources of information in Word with [Mendeley ](https://www.mendeley.com/) plugin for citations and the same `apa.csl` style, I get what I expect:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12725868/49825867-230c6b80-fd8e-11e8-98ff-8ace74d70241.png)

In lines 714-717 of `apa.csl` it is written, that the bibliography list elements should be sorted by author's name:

```xml
    <sort>
      <key macro="author" names-min="8" names-use-first="6"/>
      <key macro="issued-sort"/>
    </sort>
```

**How could this issue  be solved?**

title: Add UI to make it clear that you can click through search results using the search tool
description:
We've been using bookdown for our RStudio admin guides (http://docs.rstudio.com) for years, but I only realized when looking at #657 that you can use the arrow keys to move between search results within a section - this isn't how search functions work in most other instances (e.g. in your browser) and it's not likely that users are going to know that it's an option unless they know that the doc was written in bookdown (and that this is how search works in bookdown!). 

It'd be great if some additional UI could be added here to add clickable arrows to make it clear that you can move up/down through the available search results, similar to how it appears when doing a simple Ctrl-F in your browser: 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2779342/49762226-27a22880-fc97-11e8-931d-3c8cfba186c6.png)

title: How do I reference a static value that is defined after it is used?
description:
I noticed that there are references to sections and footnotes, but I am wondering how I do the reference in general.  For example:

I want to reference a flextable, but the typical captioning doesn't seem compatible with it, so I would like to have a separate counter be entered into something like ``[ `r nextTable()` ][tableLabel] ``, where the value returned by nextTable() (say, "Table 2.4"), would be referenced by tableLabel, so something like `` \@ref(tableLabel) `` would return "Table 2.4".  I can do this in R, but not for references made before the creation of the table.  Since Markdown does allow for similar references for sections and footnotes, is there something more general and open-ended that could be done for the flextable example I mentioned?

title: Support SVG graphics in PDF output
description:
As of https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/commit/6b72c5e35ba9b0872704b77b2bd8793657adcaba (2017), Pandoc automatically uses `rsvg-convert` to convert SVG images for PDF outputs. This allows

    ![Caption](nice-image.svg)

to produce high-quality content for both web and PDF. However, Pandoc does not do this conversion when the output format is LaTeX. (Perhaps it should, since `\includegraphics{nice-image.svg}` is known to not work.) Anyway, if I change bookdown's pandoc command from the generated

    pandoc ... --to latex --output the-book.tex

to

    pandoc ... --output the-book.pdf

then my SVG graphics process correctly and look good. Is this "direct to PDF" something that Bookdown can support, or is it unavoidable for it to process the tex output?

title: bookdown::render_book vs. rmarkdown::render_site to build all outputs
description:
I asked this question on StackOverflow a week ago and have not yet gotten a response: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/53309328/bookdownrender-book-vs-rmarkdownrender-site-to-build-all-outputs

> I've got a Bookdown book for which I'd like to build a GitBook site as well as PDF and EPUB downloads. I will use Travis to build all 3 outputs, and the PDF and EPUB will be available for download from the GitBook site.
> 
> The `bookdown-demo` calls `bookdown::render_book` once for each output in [_build.sh][1].
> 
> However, according to the logs in RStudio, the `Build Book` button, when building `All Formats`, uses `rmarkdown::render_site(encoding = 'UTF-8')` to build all outputs in a single command.
> 
> I'd like to ensure what happens on my CI server is exactly what happens in my IDE, so it seems like I should have Travis call `rmarkdown::render_site` rather than several invocations of `bookdown::render_book` as is done by the `bookdown-demo`. However, Yihui is the expert, and he has chosen to use the latter approach.
> 
> So, my question: what is the best script to invoke on a continuous integration server like Travis when multiple outputs will be built?
> 
>   [1]: https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown-demo/blob/master/_build.sh

title: Conditional compilation of chunks breaks on Travis
description:
I tried to add a cover image to the bookdown demo over at https://github.com/hammer/test-book/issues/2 and was surprised to see that the image worked in a local build but not on Travis.

After a bit of debugging, it turns out Travis doesn't like the use of `knitr:::pandoc_to()` as recommended in [issues](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/issues/168#issuecomment-238001368) and [examples](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/blob/master/inst/examples/index.Rmd#L43).

I haven't gotten around to debugging just why this triple colon operator behaves differently on my local machine versus on Travis, but I thought it might be worth noting this issue for future users.

I also think a non-private interface to allow for conditional compilation would be a good idea. Is there a reason some of the functions like `is_html_output` are in `utils.R` and not exported by `knitr`?

title: [feature request] Allow users to choose between gitbook tables & bootstrap tables
description:
gitbook's table style is quite basic comparing with tables in bootstrap. I'm wondering if it's a good idea to give people option to switch between these two styles. Right now the entire gitbook css is loaded as a whole chunk. Even if I load bootstap table style after, since existing css settings cannot be reverted, some bootstrap features (like hovering effects) cannot be displayed correctly (See https://haozhu233.github.io/kableExtra/bookdown/use-bootstrap-tables-in-gitbooks-epub.html#gitbook). 

I'm thinking if it's possible to make some modifications to the gitbook css and separate out the table part. At the same time, put bootstrap 3's table part (See [this](https://getbootstrap.com/docs/3.3/customize/) or [that](https://github.com/haozhu233/kableExtra/blob/master/inst/bootstrapTable-3.3.7/bootstrapTable.min.css)) into the resource list and create some options to switch between these two in [gitbook_dependency](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/blob/b6b96b629c78e71f0ed47db9bfead389ba5fe09a/R/gitbook.R#L75-L90). Both gitbook and bootstrap are under MIT so I guess it's okay to mix them two together. 

```
bookdown::gitbook:
    bootstrap_table: true/false
```

title: How to add custom Gitbook files declared in gitbook.r
description:
Hi there,

I am having trouble adding a custom `plugin-search.js` file to my Gitbook. I modified the contents of the `plugin-search.js` file in the package (located in `/resources/gitbook/js`) and want to add and declare it as a custom file in my `js` folder.

I created a `js` folder, a custom HTML file called `custom-search.html`, and declared it in the `_output.yml` by doing the following:

```
  includes:
      after_body: custom-search.html
```

My `custom-search.html` file contains the javascript declaration `<script src="js/plugin-search.js"></script>`.

When I build the book it adds the `<script src="js/plugin-search.js"></script>` before the closing of the `<body>` tag, but this does not override the default `<script src="libs/gitbook-2.6.7/js/plugin-search.js"></script>`.

The only other solution I can think of is loading a custom `gitbook.r` file and modifying the relevant source location below:

```r
gitbook_dependency = function() {
  assets = bookdown_file('resources', 'gitbook')
  owd = setwd(assets); on.exit(setwd(owd), add = TRUE)
  app = if (file.exists('js/app.min.js')) 'app.min.js' else 'app.js'
  list(jquery_dependency(), htmltools::htmlDependency(
    'gitbook', '2.6.7', src = assets,
    stylesheet = file.path('css', c(
      'style.css', 'plugin-bookdown.css', 'plugin-highlight.css',
      'plugin-search.css', 'plugin-fontsettings.css'
    )),
    script = file.path('js', c(
      app, 'lunr.js', 'plugin-search.js', 'plugin-sharing.js',
      'plugin-fontsettings.js', 'plugin-bookdown.js', 'jquery.highlight.js'
    ))
  ))
}
```

The actual change to `plugin-search.js` increases the accessibility of the search function by adding a `<label>` to assist screen readers. If you are interested, I can submit a pull request. You can [view my changes on my Bookdown fork](https://github.com/rblades/bookdown/commit/29b712b98e20999da53c1876833d69006390beed#diff-94e02de0c02f82929bafd95e0f4d3c9c).

Many thanks,

Rob

title: Images don't appear in html_book with special chunk names
description:
The move_files_html function (https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/blob/c470a52049b9eab7288b942bd4a065e517b3997d/R/html.R#L890) doesn't expand URL encoded links.

This means that it will not find resources with escaped characters (e.g. if the path contains a space) and thus not copy them. As a result, non self-contained books will have broken image links for plots with certain chunk names such as

    ```{r this will not show}
    ggplot(iris, aes(x = Petal.Length, y = Petal.Width, color = Species)) + geom_point()
    ```

Will not properly display the graphics in a bookdown site.

title: Use rmarkdown files as second-level heading
description:
In bookdown when using `index.Rmd` and multiple Rmd files, using knitr and merge (`new_session: yes`), the render function expect each Rmd file to be starting with first-level heading. This means that Rmarkdown files isolation happens for each _chapter_ / _top level section_. The functionality I am looking for is to have multiple chapters (top level sections) and fill them with sub-sections defined, each in an Rmd file. In short instead of `1 rmarkdown = 1 chapter` I would like to have `1 rmarkdown = 1 sub-section of a chapter`, so multiple rmarkdown files forms single chapter.

I am able to achieve that by using following structure
```
index.Rmd
0100_chapter1.Rmd           # first-level header
0101_chapter1_topic1.Rmd    ## second-level header
0101_chapter1_topic2.Rmd    ## second-level header
0200_chapter2.Rmd           # first-level header
0201_chapter2_topic1.Rmd    ## second-level header
0202_chapter2_topic2.Rmd    ## second-level header
```

but I am getting following warning:
```sh
Rscript -e 'bookdown::render_book("index.Rmd", "bookdown::gitbook")'
#Warning message:
#In split_chapters(output, gitbook_page, number_sections, split_by,  :
#  You have 7 Rmd input file(s) but only 3 first-level heading(s). Did you forget first-level headings in certain Rmd files?
Rscript -e 'packageVersion("bookdown")'
#[1] '0.7.17'
```

and while this works fine, the warning message means that it is not what it was designed to do. Therefore it can suddenly stop working with bookdown update. What is the best/recommended way to achieve this kind of modularity: sub-sections of chapters as rmarkdown files?

title: Declaration of a (ref:textreference) sometimes mistakenly detected inside a paragraph
description:
The specification says that definitions of text references should start their own paragraph.  However, this is not checked during parsing (at least for LaTeX output), so a reference which occurs within a paragraph (even in the middle of a line of the source file) is sometimes detected as a definition.  Apparently this is because the text of paragraphs is reflowed at some earlier part of the rendering process.  In cases where the actual definition occurs later in the file than the reference (I love that this is possible!) then the definition and reference are switched.

```Rmarkdown
---
title: "MWD"
output: bookdown::pdf_document2
---

Here is an example of a paragraph which includes some spacer text,
then (ref:test) and some additional text which follows it.

(ref:test) _the test text_
```

Gives the warning:
```
Warning message:
In parse_ref_links(x, "^%s (.+)$") :
  Possibly duplicated text reference labels: (ref:test)
```

and renders as:

>Here is an example of  a paragraph which includes some spacer text, then
>
> and some additional text which follows it. _the test text_

instead of the desired:

>Here is an example of a paragraph which includes some spacer text, then _the test text_ and some additional text which follows it.

title: rmd_files not respected
description:
If you have `rmd_files` specified in your `_bookdown.yml` config, but a few other Rmd files in the folder that are not listed, they now all get used due to https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/commit/38338ba085b9d15383fe1bc71c86732e129d1742. In other words, `rmd_files` is no longer respected. I think this can be easily fixed by the change proposed at 
https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/commit/38338ba085b9d15383fe1bc71c86732e129d1742#r30012237

But perhaps that would break something else, so I am just pointing it out rather than doing a PR. I can give you the PR if you prefer.

title: `bookdown`/`rmarkdown`/`knitr`: Non-code sequential processing howto?
description:
This comes from an earlier [post](https://stackoverflow.com/q/51387098/2103880) to stackoverflow ...

Programatically my `bookdown` project proceeds as follows:

 1. Reading in raw data - produces all kind of stats.
 2. Data preprocessing (logarithmization, normalization, imputation) - produces various plots for monitoring the population-level defects incurred.
 3. PCA for analysis QC - produces plots for PCA and loadings-dominating data points.
 4. Differential expression analysis - produces volcano plots and plots characterizing prominent differentially expressed features.
 5. Overrepresentation analysis of the differentially expressed features from 4. in various biological ontology systems - produces example bar plots for enriched categories.

I have analysis and narrative nicely integrated using `bookdown`, enabling efficient on fly discarding of temporary (sizable) data sets/`ggplot2` objects (pre/post transformation data etc.).

HOWEVER: The target audience is mostly/only interested in 4. & 5., leading me to the aspired to following structure:

> 4., 5., Appendix(1., 2., 3.) 

Is there any other way but precomputing 1.-5. and then revisiting in the targeted order - I would prefer to avoid accumulating all those `ggplot2` objects in memory if at all possible.

See https://github.com/lorenzwalthert/bookdown-demo/commit/d9bcee01fe7a78c505f90d618dda8a832858d311#diff-b5352b26567fa5f42ad7241975ba203bR6 for the commit where I added the option. If you remove the line and re-build the book, you will see that the template again takes effect. Otherwise the option seems to work fine. I don't understand what's going on. Any help appreciated.

title: Equations not rendered using html_book
description:
I have an `index.Rmd` file that looks like this.

```
--- 
title: "This is a title"
author: "Mr. Author"
date: "Today"
site: bookdown::bookdown_site
documentclass: book
output:
  bookdown::html_book
---

$y = \sqrt{x}$
```
When I build my book the equation in the file is not rendered. Nevertheless, should I choose `gitbook` as the output instead of `html_book` then the equation is rendered just fine. I also do not have a problem rendering the equation when knitting an `html_document` rather than `html_book`, such as below:

```
---
title: "This is a title"
author: "Mr. Author"
date: "Today"
output: html_document
---

$y = \sqrt{x}$
```
Can others reproduce this issue? If so, is this behaviour by design or a bug?

title: eqnarray environment does not work with ```pdf_book()```
description:
The following bookdown document (called ```index.Rmd```) works with the output format ```gitbook()```, but not with the output format ```pdf_book()```.

````
# Bug

Here's an aligned equation:

$$
\begin{eqnarray}
x =& y \\
y =& z \\
\end{eqnarray}
$$
````
Running the following command works and gives the expected html output:

```r
> bookdown::render_book("index.Rmd", output_format=bookdown::gitbook())
```

But running the following command gives an error:

```r
> bookdown::render_book("index.Rmd", output_format=bookdown::pdf_book())

.... processing messages ...

! Missing \endgroup inserted.
<inserted text> 
                \endgroup 
l.97 \begin{eqnarray}

Error: Failed to compile _main.tex. See _main.log for more info.
Please delete _main.Rmd after you finish debugging the error.
```

The reason for the error is clear enough -- the file ```_main.tex``` has wrapped the ```\begin{eqnarray} ... \end{eqnarray}``` environment in ```\[``` and ```\]```.  The file ```_main.tex``` contains the following tex:

````
% ... preamble stuff...

\section{Bug}\label{bug}}

Here's an aligned equation:

\[
\begin{eqnarray}
x =& y \\
y =& z \\
\end{eqnarray}
\]

\end{document}

````

If I delete  ```\[``` and ```\]``` and manually run ```pdflatex _main.tex```, it compiles fine.  (NB: ```pdflatex``` also fails on the original version of ```_main.tex``` from the command line.)

I observed a similar problem with the ```align``` environment.  Other math mode environments probably have the same problem.

title: Centrer des titres
description:
For general questions, please ask them on StackOverflow first, using the tags `r` and `bookdown`: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/ask Please come back here only if nobody answers your question there, and let us know the URL of your StackOverflow post. If you are not sure whether to post a StackOverflow question or open a Github issue, do the former first.

For bug reports, please try the development version first: `devtools::install_github('rstudio/bookdown')`. If it still does not work, please provide a minimal, self-contained, and reproducible example by reducing your example as much as possible right before the problem goes away. By doing this, you may be able to figure out what the problem really is before reporting to me. You can attach your example as a zip file here, and screenshots are often very helpful to illustrate your issues. You may consider creating your reproducible example based on https://github.com/yihui/bookdown-minimal. Please include the following info with your bug report:

```{r}
devtools::session_info('bookdown')
rmarkdown::pandoc_version()
system('pdflatex --version')
```

To include a verbatim chunk of arbitrary text, enclose it in four backticks, especially when the text contains backticks, e.g.

````
A sample document.

```{r}
1 + 1  # a line of code
```

Another paragraph.
````

If it is just a chunk of R code (or other languages) and you want syntax highlighting, you may use three backticks to format it, e.g.

```r
rnorm(10)
```

Usually your issue will be closed after it is fixed, but sometimes it is closed only because we are not able to offer any help. It does not mean your issue is not real or bad. You can propose a fix by yourself through a pull request. Your constructive feedback is always appreciated.

title: feature request: option to restart endnote numbering after each GitBook-style web chapter
description:

I am preparing an historical book manuscript, written in R-Markdown with Bookdown, which will have 8 chapters, each with 100+ Chicago-style endnotes, using the GitBook-style web format.

My goal is to restart endnote numbering after each chapter, to avoid running into high digits and to resemble the appearance of traditional history books.

title: pandoc2+gitbook give excessive margin after code blocks
description:
Using yihui/knitr@v1.20, rstudio/rmarkdown@v1.9, and rstudio/bookdown@v0.7.

Given a code block with leading and trailing text like the following:

````
It is also possible to specify the list of email attachments from R code.
For example:

```r
attachments <- list("attachment_1.csv", "attachment_2.csv")
rmarkdown::output_metadata$set(rsc_email_attachments = attachments)
```

An email attachment will be accessible via HTTP just like an output file, and
you can make a link to it in your report in the same way.
````

When using pandoc-1.19.2.1, it renders like:
![screen shot 2018-04-06 at 2 43 32 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/362187/38438645-175fa076-39a9-11e8-9100-67a83028edda.png)

Switching to pandoc-2.1.3, we get:
![screen shot 2018-04-06 at 2 43 47 pm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/362187/38438661-236c3942-39a9-11e8-8db6-c41b28a42189.png)

This is because pandoc is injecting `sourceCode` margins:

```
div.sourceCode { margin: 1em 0; }
```

and gitbook is also doing something similar:

```
.book .book-body .page-wrapper .page-inner section.normal pre{overflow:auto;word-wrap:normal;margin:0 0 1.275em;padding:.85em 1em;background:#f7f7f7}
```

title: Broken less frequently used types of cross-references / links
description:
Ir R `bookdown` I use tags `(\#tab:table-1)`, `(\#exr:exr-1)` and `\@ref(tab:table-1)`, `\@ref(exr:exr-1)` etc. to create links between objects in my book.

Links, that include `tab:`, `fig:`, `eq:` work as expected.
Other less frequently used types of links, such as `exr:`, `cor:`, do not work.

Example. I created a new `bookdown` project (minimal bookdown example) in RStudio and called it `tmp_bookdown`. I used **Gitbook** format. In the file `01-intro.Rmd` I wrote the following code:


```
# Links

Table \@ref(tab:table-1), exercise \@ref(exr:exr-1), equation \@ref(eq:equation-1), etc. \@ref(cor:cor-1).


# Data

: (\#tab:table-1)

my    table
--  --------
0       4

(\#exr:exr-1) First exercise. 

(\#cor:cor-1) Sth. else.

\begin{equation} 
  EX = \frac{q}{p}
  (\#eq:equation-1)
\end{equation} 
```	

The contents of web page `links.htlm`:


[![enter image description here][1]][1]


When I click on the links, the address in the address bar changed as follows:

 * Link "Table 3.1" → address "tmp_bookdown/_book/data.html#tab:table-1" → link works;
 * Link "exercise 3.1" → address "tmp_bookdown/_book/links.html#exr:exr-1" → link is **broken**;
 * Link "equation (3.1)" → address "tmp_bookdown/_book/data.html#eq:equation-1" → link works;
 * Link "etc. 3.1" → address "tmp_bookdown/_book/links.html#cor:cor-1" → link is **broken**.

In `data.html` I did not find neither "cor:" nor "exr:". It seems that no anchors are created for these.

title: request: new behavior of gitbook toc collapse
description:
First, love the package thanks!

The collapse setting for gitbook is great, but currently it takes two clicks on a collapsed heading to unfurl it if the heading is also a separate html page. If you click on the TOC element that is collapsed, and the page loads, it will not unfurl unless the heading is clicked on again. `collapse: section` with `split_by: section` for instance says that on page load it should be collapsed, but in the case of a direct click on the heading leading to a page load, it would be natural for the clicked section to unfurl.

Another idea would be to have any section unfurl whenever a section is highlighted as in `scroll_highlight: yes` regardless of whether it is clicked on or not. A sensible default would imho be that currently viewed content should be unfurled in the TOC, while content that is not on screen should be furled.

Sorry if this is doable already, and thanks in advance for your advice!

title: Trailing spaces within examples in Sec. 2.2.1
description:
Hi. 

I was wondering why there are trailing spaces in the sample code in [Section 2.2.1](https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/markdown-extensions-by-bookdown.html#equations) of the book - specifically, the space after `\begin{equation}` and `\end{equation}`. 
It seems like they were [deliberately added](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/commit/82aed3e65d50ff6643b175b493a2518a392e3831) but I couldn't decipher the commit message. 

The reason this came up is because the sample code fails to run using `bookdown::word_document2` - a document is produced, but the equations do not show up (not an issue for html or pdf output).
This is a quirk of Word output - there can't be anything after `...{equation}` as mentioned in #190 - and I was able to get the equation to show by removing the trailing spaces.
But I'm still left wondering why the trailing space was there in the first place.

Here's sample code with trailing spaces which doesn't render properly.
```
---
output:
  bookdown::word_document2
---

\begin{equation} 
  f\left(k\right) = \binom{n}{k} p^k\left(1-p\right)^{n-k}
  (\#eq:binom) 
\end{equation} 

Equation \@ref(eq:binom) is the probability mass function of the binomial distribution with size parameter $n$ and success probability $p$. 
```

title: Supporting short figure/table captions for list of figures/tables
description:
The captions of figures or tables often need to be long in order to provide the reader with an accurate explanation about what is being shown.
To prevent the list of figures from becoming too difficult to read, LaTeX is offering an optional argument in the `\caption[short description for list of figures/tables]{Here comes the full explanation, which can consist of multiple sentences. This is particularly useful when having multiple subfigures.}`.
As far as I can see, there is no way to map a figure caption written in R Markdown/knitr to this macro.
However, I think this would be both, helpful and technically feasible.
Please note that there is already some discussion in the development of pandoc to implement such a feature (<https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/issues/2417>).

title: Markdown syntax figures not appearing in list of figures
description:
Figures included with `knitr::include_graphics()` inside an R code chunk appear in the list of figures, but
figures included with the markdown syntax `![caption](images/img1.png)` to my experience don't.
Since one can always use the call to knitr, this is actually not a very urgent issue. If others can replicate this for me unexpected behaviour, it might be worth mentioning it in the documentation.

title: equation numbering not working for epub output format
description: Hello, first I would like to thank you all for this incredible package you have put together. I am a university professor and I believe it is transformative and certainly is a fantastic tool for reproducible research. I have started asking my students to write everything in R markdown, and I would like to ask them to write their thesis in bookdown...?!! I am not a Latex person, I try to be an `R` one. Now, I have started to use bookdown to write a textbook for my classes. And I have stumbled upon an issue with equations. After many hours spent to find my mistakes, I decided to copy and paste equation 2.2 from the bookdown manual (https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/). So, for this I copy the exact code below in the `02-literature.Rmd` document and I clicked `Build Book`. ``` # Literature Here is a review of existing methods. $$ \begin{align} g(X_{n}) &= g(\theta)+g'({\tilde{\theta}})(X_{n}-\theta) \notag \\ \sqrt{n}[g(X_{n})-g(\theta)] &= g'\left({\tilde{\theta}}\right) \sqrt{n}[X_{n}-\theta ] (\#eq:align) \end{align} $$ ``` And I get this message: ``` output file: bookdown-demo.knit.md ! Package amsmath Error: Erroneous nesting of equation structures; (amsmath) trying to recover with `aligned'. Error: Failed to compile bookdown-demo.tex. See bookdown-demo.log for more info. ``` So, as I was writing this I solved one issue and I suggest this becomes written on the bookdown manual. The manual could be clearer by saying that if one wants to reference equations, DO NOT USE `$$` before or after the equation like I have in the code above. This could save many hours of frustration to many people. By the way, the code above will work for `gitbook` output but not `pdf_book` output. Looking back in the manual, the `$$` are not there, but they are on the previous page/part 2.1.3. So, if I may suggest so, adding this warning on top of part 2.2 would be great! I did find one issue, which is that the `epub` output will not number the equation using this code: ```# Literature Here is a review of existing methods. \begin{align} g(X_{n}) &= g(\theta)+g'({\tilde{\theta}})(X_{n}-\theta) \\ \sqrt{n}[g(X_{n})-g(\theta)] &= g'\left({\tilde{\theta}}\right) \sqrt{n}[X_{n}-\theta ] (\#eq:align) \end{align} ``` it yields: Thanks again for your fantastic contribution to all, and certainly my field! Best.

title: Child documents and path definition in `YAML` headers
description:
This is asked [here](https://stackoverflow.com/q/47654521/2103880) first a month ago without any takers, so I try here again ... 

I'm building a reporting infrastructure that makes extensive use of child documents (via `{r, child = 'somedir/child_doc.Rmd'}`) AND is parametrized through the `params` dictionary in the `YAML` header of the master document. An example might be:

    ---
    title: Project Report
    subtitle: POIGNANT DESCRIPTION OF THE WORK AT HAND
    date: '`r format(Sys.time(), "%d %B, %Y")`'
    output:
      bookdown::pdf_document2:
        template: ~
        toc: yes
        toc_depth: 2
    colorlinks: yes
    fontsize: 11pt
    documentclass: scrartcl
    geometry: margin=1in, a4paper
    params:
      submodule:
        value:
          intro:
            data_dir: 'data'
    ---

Using this structure, accessing `data_dir` becomes problematic as the working directory differs for the master and child documents and thus relative path definitions also diverge. Ways out are:

1. Usage of absolute/expanded path names in defining `data_dir`. **Gets long/unwieldy quickly.**

2. Postprocessing of the `params` object to expand the path within the master document. As `params` is immutable when accessed from within `R` chunks, this can only be solved in an **inelegant** manner:

        ```{r params-processing, include = FALSE}
        local_params <- params
        local_params$submodule$intro$data_dir <- path.expand(local_params$submodule$intro$data_dir)
Followed by internal usage of `local_params` instead of `params`.

3. In-place expansion of the path using something like `!R path.expand('data')` when defining the parameter in the `YAML` header. While this (or the \`-based equivalent) works for the `data` field in the example, `knitr`ing **fails** in the path case as the `R` expression is *not* expanded but used as a character-representation - and literal `"path.expand('data')"` obviously doesn't exist as a path.

I'd appreciate any hints on how to solve this prettily - especially whether 3. can be made work ...

title: Bookdown Gitbook only generating 1 page (can't navigate to view other pages)
description:
[Link to Stack Overflow question](https://stackoverflow.com/q/48305419/9129593)
I've been having trouble building a bookdown book into Gitbook. I downloaded the bookdown-demo, opened the RStudio project, and used the Build Pane to build all formats.

This appears to generate the PDF and EPUB outputs with no issues, but the navigation bar in the Gitbook don't work and all I can see are the book's cover page. title: using `code` at end of title invalidates {-}
Cross-reference equations, figures and tables when bookdown is NOT already installed?
description:
This question is identical to [this question](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/47794311/knitr-cross-reference-equations-figures-and-tables-when-bookdown-is-not-alread) that I posted on StackOverflow last month, but for which I didn't get a satisfactory answer. Apologies for the duplication. I'm posting here because I suspect the most elegant solution might be to handle this issue in RStudio, as I will explain later. I hope this might also kick-start some activity in this direction.

I'm aware that the canonical method for cross-referencing figures and tables in a PDF produced by knitr is to use `bookdown::pdf_document2`.

*This is awesome!* But suppose that I want to send my Rmd to a user who doesn't have **bookdown** already installed? How can I ensure that the document will render if knitted in an environment in which **bookdown** is not already installed? I want to have everything self-contained in a single Rmd file. The consumer of the document might be someone with little or no prior experience of R, and has just installed R and RStudio but no packages. How can I ensure that if they click **knit** that they will get the PDF with cross-references? Alternatively, what if Binder or similar provide the means to execute (or, better still, knit to PDF) Rmd files in much the same way as is done with Jupyter Notebooks -- I'd like to be able to bundle everything that is needed for rendering the PDF in an automated way in the Rmd file itself.

An example document looks like this:

    ---
    title: "Cross-refs test"
    author: "Me"
    date: "13 December 2017"
    output:
      bookdown::pdf_document2:
        citation_package: natbib
        fig_caption: yes
        keep_tex: yes
    ---

    ```{r setup, include=FALSE}
    knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
    ```

    ## Title

    \begin{equation}
    f\left(k\right)=\binom{n}{k}p^k\left(1-p\right)^{n-k} \label{eq:binom}
    \end{equation}

    You may refer to it using `\@ref(eq:binom)`, e.g., see Equation \@ref(eq:binom).

So if this Rmd file is downloaded and knit by a brain-dead zombie, or by Binder, how can I make sure that this doesn't happen:

    Error in loadNamespace(name) : there is no package called 'bookdown'
    Calls: <Anonymous> ... tryCatch -> tryCatchList -> tryCatchOne -> <Anonymous>
    Execution halted

I can't assume that a consumer of my Rmd will know what to do in this situation, nor any automated process that I don't control that renders a PDF from the Rmd that it grabs from a repo somewhere (like what Binder does).

If there are *no* cross-references, I can specify `pdf_document` as the output format and RStudio will read the YAML and if **knitr** and **rmarkdown** are not installed, installation of these will be triggered automatically (the user/brain-dead zombie just has to click on "OK" to accept installation) and the PDF will be rendered. So if these two packages are missing: no problem, at least when using RStudio. User gets Rmd, installs R and Rstudio, knits the Rmd, and the PDF appears. The same is not true if using **bookdown** to get cross-referencing.

It seems the YAML is interpreted before R code is executed, so the same kind of logic as this that is used to print the current time in a document (``` date: "`r Sys.time()`"```) doesn't work. Otherwise, I'd `r install.packages("bookdown")` here.

So, is there a method to do cross-referencing without bookdown, but as simply and as elegantly as with bookdown, or is there someway of triggering knitr to install bookdown such that rendering won't crash when encountering `bookdown::pdf_document2`?

Basically, what I want is cross-references in a knitted PDF with minimal user intervention to make it happen -- 'cos my user might be a brain-dead zombie or robot.

I want to avoid hard-coding cross-refs. And I'd rather not use LaTeX. Just pure R Markdown and some knitr magic, if possible.

A possible solution to this issue would be for RStudio to recognise instances of bookdown::pdf_document2 in the YAML and trigger installation of bookdown, in the same way that the user is prompted to install knitr and rmarkdown if they are not already present: they need only click a button to proceed and complete the process of rendering the document. It would appear that this would be the most elegant solution. If this is not possible, what's the next best solution?

Thanks!

title: `render_book()` should not delete custom config files
description:
I just tried the new custom config option, and I noticed that `render_book()` temporarily deletes my custom config file and also overwrites my default `_bookdown.yml` file. If all goes well, things are restored properly at the end of the compile, but if anything goes wrong (R crashes, pandoc crashes, power goes out, whatever) then this can lead to data loss. Also, if I have either my custom config file or my `_bookdown.yml` open in RStudio then RStudio will detect the changes and inform me the file has been deleted or reload the file, respectively.

This issue is conceptually related to #405. The bookdown package should not touch any source files whatsoever.

The correct way to handle all these issues, I think, would be to copy all the source files into a temporary directory and do the compile there.

but I get misnumbering / mangling of the non-previewed sections when I attempt to use `preview_chapter`, `render_book` with `preview=TRUE` and `serve_book`.

title: Section References when Section Number is chosen as FALSE
description:
Thanks for the great package!

I have created a MWE to demonstrate the oddity I have found.
When  number_sections: FALSE in the _output.yml the LaTeX file generated by the bookdown build process does not display the section. 

To demonstrate I have uploaded my MWE. In this, you will find two identical examples except in the one I have number_sections: FALSE and the sectioned is not referenced and in the other number_sections: TRUE the section is referenced with the section number. 

[bookdown MWP - Ref.zip](https://github.com/rstudio/bookdown/files/1555755/bookdown.MWP.-.Ref.zip)

I know this problem could exist in the way that the LaTeX referencing works (when bookdown has set the section levels = 0.) Nonetheless, just because one does not want section numbers, should not limit one's ability to reference sections.

I propose a solution like this:
If Section Numbers are FALSE, then authors would most likely want to reference on the section title. 
One could use the LaTeX package:
\usepackage{nameref}
%Which would do the following:
 \section{Evolution of Bookdown}\label{sec:Chpt1}

Where when LaTeX processes 
`This package allows the title associated with the anchor to be used \nameref{sec:Chpt1}
`
The output is:
This package allows the title associated with the anchor to be used Evolution of Bookdown.

This could be resolved by:
1. adding the nameref package to the LaTeX preamble
2. By changing \ref{} to \nameref{} for those who chose number_sections: FALSE

Let me know if I can help.

title: Bibliography issue
description:
I had a problem with my .bib files that were working fine for months in the same bookdown project, and eventually started to throw an error (same Windows 10 platform.)  While not strictly a bookdown issue, I think it merits a table or a few words in the documentation and maybe a warning somewhere.

`
This is BibTeX, Version 0.99d (MiKTeX 2.9.6500 64-bit)
The top-level auxiliary file: bookdown-demo.aux
The style file: apalike.bst
White space in argument---line 35 of file bookdown-demo.aux
 : \bibdata{book,packages,music\protect
 :                                      \TU\textunderscore report3}
I'm skipping whatever remains of this command
`

In this case, the `music_report3.bib` file worked fine with the whole workflow, from RStudio via RMarkDown, knitr, pandoc, MiKTeX until some updates, when the underscore somehow inserted a whitespace somewhere.  I was introduced to LaTeX by the fantastic bookdown package, but not being familiar with these workflow elements, it took me a lot of time to find out about this.  I had been using this project for months without problem. Now renaming this file to `musicreport3.bib` solved the problem. In hindsight it is trivial, but after it had been working... 

However, this is not the only issue.  Certain characters, such as the normal-hyphen caused problems with chunks, and references.

I think it would be a good idea to somewhere summarize (and add warnings) to avoidable characters in chunks, refs, file names.  My experience shows, that at least on windows, anything that goes beyond the ASCII latin alphabet and digits is a danger zone somewhere.

•

title: R code inside HTML comments is executed
description:
@raphywink and me were just trying to debug why our book could not be built, when we noticed that commenting out lines in our Rmd files does not have the desired effect. The code inside is still executed.

I have forked bookdown-minimal (see https://github.com/MJochim/bookdown-demo) to illustrate the point.

Let's say you have a document like this:

````
A sample document. With some faulty code integrated:

```{r}
nonExistentFunction()
```

Another paragraph.
````

You notice the code is faulty and want to do away with it. You comment it out:

````
A sample document. With some faulty code integrated:

<!--
```{r}
nonExistentFunction()
```
-->
Another paragraph.
````

Now what I would expect is that the output contains the comment with the literal code inside.

But what happens is, the output contains the comment and inside the comment is the result of the **evaluated faulty code**. In our case, the code errored out and the book could not be built at all.

In my opinion, this behavior is very odd. After all (R)Markdown is supposed to be based on HTML and should therefore respect HTML comments.

---

You are asking to provide information about my R session with the bug report, but I think in this case, they would not be helpful, so I will omit them. If you think otherwise, I can of course add them.

```{r}
devtools::session_info('bookdown')
rmarkdown::pandoc_version()
system('pdflatex --version')
```

title: Crossreference syntax
description:
I have a comment on table cross-referencing. 
 I kept puzzling over the meaning of the last paragraph of Section 2.5 (Tables) of the bookdown ebook. 

I have worked up a functioning skeleton here that does captions and cross-references for tables and figures. It tests both inline rchunks as well as testing a separate rchunk file. Both are now working fine. 

See: https://github.com/aetiologicCanada/matthew_default_bookdown

Tables captions appear to require syntax such as:
------ begin here
# Tables with R chunks

 ```{r foo4, tidy=TRUE, echo=FALSE, cache=FALSE}```
 Table: (\#tab:foo4) Caption TableRchunk Goes Here 

Here we reference the  table: \@ref(tab:foo4)
---- end here -----
Lines such as:

**Table: (\#tab:foo4) Caption TableRchunk Goes Here** 

are needed to generate table captions and referencing but these lines are neither "text" in the usual sense, nor are the lines traditional "R code."   It seems to be that they violate the clear distinction needed between R code and text in an Rmd file, and some reconsideration is needed. Perhaps it would be clearly if these lines could be placed within code chunks or were transformed into classical R functions that could be called from the Rmd file. 

Some rationalization of how the code works for this problem, and a rewrite of Section 2.5 would be most helpful.
